item.title: Stephen A Smith says what he saw from one team during NFL Week 10 was ‘Super Bowl material’
item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With yet another week of NFL action almost in the books, Stephen A. Smith pointed out the team that impressed him the most. The NFL season is well past the halfway mark, and the true contenders in the league are becoming clearer with each passing week. However, there is one team that stood out the most to Stephen A. Smith after their Week 10 performance, and he believes they have shown him another level. Stephen A. Smith claims Minnesota Vikings’ defence is ‘something to behold’ Speaking on his podcast, Stephen A. Smith praised the Minnesota Vikings for their intense defensive effort against Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. He pointed out how DC Brian Flores has been able to turn the defensive unit into one of the most dangerous in the NFL, and warned the rest of the league that they are true Super Bowl contenders. “I’m here to tell you right now – the Minnesota Vikings are a Super Bowl contender,” Stephen A. Smith said on his podcast. “That defence is something to behold. The loss yesterday was not on Jordan Love. I get it. Minnesota was all over them like white on rice. That defence was absolutely, positively, nightmarish. “Jordan Love faced a career-high 60% pressure rate, taking eight sacks and 12 hits. 11/13 Vikings defenders who had a pass rush generated pressure, with nine defenders having multiple pressures. Jordan Love lost more yards (59) on sacks than the Packers gained rushing the football (56). That is an annihilation. In the two games he has faced Minnesota this year, he has been sacked 12 times and hit 27 times… “This defence, led by Brian Flores, is legit; it’s real. In order to beat the Minnesota Vikings, you gotta be able to run the football. There is no way around it. If you can not run the football against the Minnesota Vikings, you’re toast.” The Vikings’ defence has been lauded all season, but their performance against the Packers this weekend showed that they have unlocked a new level. And after solving their QB woes by trading for Kirk Cousins, the Vikings are a team with very few standout weaknesses, and could be Super Bowl-bound. Read more: What Stephen A. Smith said he ‘couldn’t resist’ doing after Cowboys loss to the 49ers Stephen A. Smith and Richard Sherman question NFL officials over CeeDee Lamb penalty Who Stephen A. Smith picked to win the Super Bowl before 26/27 season began

item.title: Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo puts Jabari Smith Jr. on a poster with epic dunk
item.description: Nov 16, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Houston Rockets forward Tari Eason (17) drives to the basket against Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) during the first quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo puts Jabari Smith Jr. on a poster with epic dunk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Giannis Antetokounmpo showed no mercy as he posterized Jabari Smith Jr. during the Miami Heat’s clash with the Houston Rockets on Monday night. Antetokounmpo has been playing in the NBA since 2013, going through his first season with the Heat. Following a slow start from the team, they have bounced back in resounding fashion as Antetokounmpo has been delivering dominant performances on the court. Going into the contest with Houston, Miami has won seven of their last nine games since starting 0-4 on the season. The strong winning form has built confidence within the team, especially with Antetokounmpo impressing many with his overall form and production. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Antetokounmpo also didn’t hesitate to unleash his dunking talent. The highlight took place in the second quarter as he competed against Smith inside the paint. He soared up to throw down the poster dunk over the standout forward, wowing the attending home fans in Miami. GIANNIS ANTETOKOUNMPO POWERS HOME THE STRONG LEFT-HANDED SLAM! JUST TOO STRONG 💪 pic.twitter.com/tea4qk1SPn — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 17, 2026 How Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat played against Rockets Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat are rolling as they took down Jabari Smith Jr. and the Rockets by a 128-110 at home. Miami set the tone against Houston early on, leading 29-15 after the first quarter. Houston never recovered from the slow start as the Heat enjoyed a strong scoring night from the entire squad. Eight players scored in double-digits for Miami in the win, including Antetokounmpo. He finished with a stat line of 20 points, 13 rebounds, six assists, three blocks, and one steal. He shot 8-of-11 from the field and 4-of-6 from the free-throw line. Klay Thompson came next with 17 points and two assists, Bobby Portis had 16 points and six rebounds, while Davion Mitchell delivered 16 points and 10 assists. Miami improved to an 8-6 record this season, sitting at fourth place in the Eastern Conference standings. They are above the Atlanta Hawks and the New York Knicks while trailing the Detroit Pistons and the Detroit Pistons. The Heat will look forward to their next matchup, remaining at home. They host the Milwaukee Bucks as tip-off commences on Nov. 18 at 7 p.m. ET. item.title: 76ers’ Jaylen Brown left bloodied after scary collision with Julius Randle
item.description: Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images 76ers’ Jaylen Brown left bloodied after scary collision with Julius Randle appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Monday, the P hiladelphia 76ers were trying to hold off the Brooklyn Nets in the fourth quarter after the Nets cut into what was once a 24-point lead for Philly. But with around nine minutes remaining in the fourth, the 76ers encountered some trouble when Jaylen Brown collided headfirst with Julius Randle’s chin — with Brown bearing the brunt of that impact. Brown received the ball on the high post area, spinning away from his defender, Nets guard Keon Ellis. Sensing danger, Randle rotated over. However, the 76ers star careened straight onto Randle, and both of them fell immediately. Brown immediately clutched onto his head after being left bloodied by the blow he took. Jaylen Brown just took a tough shot to the head bumping into Julius Randle here. He's bleeding from the forehead, but got up and walked to the bench on his own power for treatment. pic.twitter.com/Rkwxh6SnE8 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Erin Grugan (@eringrugan) November 17, 2026 Brown is band in the back on the bench applying pressure to his head. He gives a thumbs up here https://t.co/DeBOq06yoQ pic.twitter.com/HB2fH7rnmM — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) November 17, 2026 Both Brown and Randle exited the game after that collision, with Tyrese Maxey and Michael Porter Jr. coming in, respectively, to relieve those two players. The good news for the 76ers was that Brown only needed to miss three minutes of game time. He returned to action with 6:02 left in the fourth, and he helped Philly keep the Nets at bay. Perhaps as a matter of precaution, the 76ers pulled Brown with 1:44 still remaining in the game. They were up by just seven at that point, and the Nets even cut the 76ers’ lead to just four on the subsequent possession, but Philly was confident enough in the talent they had out on the court that they could afford to give Brown a few extra minutes of rest. Brown was phenomenal for the 76ers on Monday. He tallied 31 points, 13 rebounds, and four assists on 9-of-19 shooting from the field, and supporting Joel Embiid in his stellar 37-point outing in what ended up being a 135-123 victory over the Nets. The 76ers have a day off tomorrow before heading to Orlando to face a Magic team that’s currently on a four-game winning streak, and it remains to be seen if Brown would be given the night off for that game. item.title: Former Champion Jorge Linares Arrested By ICE Agents Monday
item.description: What to Know Four-time world champion Jorge Linares announced via social media early on Monday, November 15, that he had been arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents at the El Paso border crossing with Mexico. The nature of the arrest is not known. A nationally known immigration law firm now represents Linares. The four-time world champion retired in 2023 and was added to the International Hall of Fame ballot this year. Fans and followers of four-time former world champion Jorge “El Nino de Oro” Linares were shocked to see a post on his X/Twitter account early on Monday morning. It was brief. Me tiene el ICE en el paso Texas. Que locura — Jorge Linares (@JorgeLinares) November 15, 2026 Linares reported he had been taken into custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at the United States / Mexican border in El Paso, Texas shortly after 8 a.m. ET/5 a.m. PT. Four-Time World Champion Jorge Linares is a four time world champion, and now on the International Boxing Hall of Fame ballot. Linares, 41, a native of Venezuela, currently resides in Miami, Florida. Widely regarded as among the most skilled and exciting boxers of his generation in the smaller weight divisions, Linares won world titles in three weight divisions in 21 years at featherweight, super featherweight, and lightweight. Linares won his first world title in 2007. He later added the WBA World Super Featherweight title in 2008, and the WBA and WBC World Lightweight titles from 2014 to 2018. Linares retired in 2023 after a loss to Jack Catterall of England in Liverpool. He retired with a record of 47-9, 29 KOs. For much of his career, Linares lived and trained in Japan. After compiling an impressive record in amateur competition, Linares left Venezuela to pursue professional boxing at age 17 in December 2002 under the management of the Teiken Boxing Gym in Tokyo, Japan, training primarily with Sendai Tanaka. After retiring in October 2023, Linares transitioned into boxing training, coaching, and managing his own gym in Miami. He also now works as a World Boxing Association (WBA) supervisor and commentator. Jorge Linares In Custody, Law Firm Reports Jorge Linares posted a photo with WBA President Gilberto Mendoza, who joined Linares to celebrate his birthday in August. Photo: @JorgeLinares/Instagram Several hours after the post about his arrest, WBA President Gilberto Mendoza posted an update, confirming that Linares was in ICE custody. Mendoza reported that immigration attorneys were handling his case. “I am in constant contact with his family. As WBA President, I will always support our champions, in and out of the ring. Stay strong, Jorge,” wrote Mendoza. A copy of the original letter posted by the law firm representing Jorge Linares after being distributed to Spanish-language media. item.content:encoded: What to Know Four-time world champion Jorge Linares announced via social media early on Monday, November 15, that he had been arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents at the El Paso border crossing with Mexico. The nature of the arrest is not known. A nationally known immigration law firm now represents Linares. The four-time world champion retired in 2023 and was added to the International Hall of Fame ballot this year. Fans and followers of four-time former world champion Jorge “El Nino de Oro” Linares were shocked to see a post on his X/Twitter account early on Monday morning. It was brief. Me tiene el ICE en el paso Texas. Que locura — Jorge Linares (@JorgeLinares) November 15, 2026 Linares reported he had been taken into custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at the United States / Mexican border in El Paso, Texas shortly after 8 a.m. ET/5 a.m. PT. Four-Time World Champion Jorge Linares is a four time world champion, and now on the International Boxing Hall of Fame ballot. Linares, 41, a native of Venezuela, currently resides in Miami, Florida. Widely regarded as among the most skilled and exciting boxers of his generation in the smaller weight divisions, Linares won world titles in three weight divisions in 21 years at featherweight, super featherweight, and lightweight. Linares won his first world title in 2007. He later added the WBA World Super Featherweight title in 2008, and the WBA and WBC World Lightweight titles from 2014 to 2018. Linares retired in 2023 after a loss to Jack Catterall of England in Liverpool. He retired with a record of 47-9, 29 KOs. For much of his career, Linares lived and trained in Japan. After compiling an impressive record in amateur competition, Linares left Venezuela to pursue professional boxing at age 17 in December 2002 under the management of the Teiken Boxing Gym in Tokyo, Japan, training primarily with Sendai Tanaka. After retiring in October 2023, Linares transitioned into boxing training, coaching, and managing his own gym in Miami. He also now works as a World Boxing Association (WBA) supervisor and commentator. Jorge Linares In Custody, Law Firm Reports Jorge Linares posted a photo with WBA President Gilberto Mendoza, who joined Linares to celebrate his birthday in August. Photo: @JorgeLinares/Instagram Several hours after the post about his arrest, WBA President Gilberto Mendoza posted an update, confirming that Linares was in ICE custody. Mendoza reported that immigration attorneys were handling his case. “I am in constant contact with his family. As WBA President, I will always support our champions, in and out of the ring. Stay strong, Jorge,” wrote Mendoza. A copy of the original letter posted by the law firm representing Jorge Linares after being distributed to Spanish-language media. Photo: RicardoCelis/X In a second update, the law firm representing Linares, immigration law specialists Wilner and O’Reilly , posted a letter confirming its role in the case. “Wilner and O’Reilly confirms that it represents Jorge “El Nino de Oro” Linares, the Venezuelan boxer and world champion, following his recent detention by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). “Mr. Linares is legally present in the United States and has fully cooperated with the authorities. We are working closely with ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to resolve this matter as quickly as possible. “Immigration processes follow established procedures, and those procedures take time. We have confidence in Mr. Linares’ position and expect this matter to be resolved once the process is complete. We ask for patience from his supporters, the press, and the public in the meantime. “Mr. Linares and his family are deeply grateful for the outpouring of support received from Venezuela and his fans around the world. Out of respect for his privacy and the legal process, we will not be commenting further on the details of his case at this time.” Given the aggressive nature of immigration enforcement in the United States under the Trump Administration, particularly with Venezuelan natives, the arrest of Linares is certainly concerning. Boxing Hall of Fame Awaits Jorge Linares Jorge Linares participated in Boxing Hall of Fame weekend last June as a former world champion. Photo: @JorgeLinares/Instagram The timing of the arrest feels even more shocking, coming just weeks after Linares became eligible and appeared on the ballot this year as a candidate for the International Boxing Hall of Fame, after waiting the three-year retirement period to become eligible. On learning about the recognition, Linares responded to a social media post, writing, “AMEN!” Last June, Linares participated in the Class of 2026 Hall of Fame Induction weekend, taking part in the traditional parade of champions through Canastota, New York. Linares posted photos and a message to his hundreds of thousands of followers. “What an incredible honor to be invited to the International Boxing Hall of Fame weekend. “Standing among the legends of boxing reminded me how blessed I have been throughout my career. I want to thank the International Boxing Hall of Fame for their hospitality, and thank all of my fans who have supported me through every victory and every challenge. “God willing, I hope to return next year, and with the support of my fans and the grace of God, I hope that one day my name will also be inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame. “Thank you for the memories, the respect, and the love. This was truly special.” Here’s hoping “El Nino de Oro” is able to join the celebration, whether as a member of the Class of 2027 or an honored guest.

item.title: Watch Rangers raise banner to celebrate 100th anniversary of first-ever game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Watch Rangers raise banner to celebrate 100th anniversary of first-ever game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Rangers marked a major milestone on Monday night, raising a banner to the rafters at Madison Square Garden to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the franchise’s first-ever game . Exactly 100 years to the day after their NHL debut, the Rangers held a special ceremony at their game against the Montreal Canadiens. The players looked on from the ice as the commemorative banner made its way up to the Garden rafters. The night served as the Rangers’ “Centennial Capstone Game,” closing out a season-long celebration of the franchise’s history. It also kicked off the NHL’s Original Six Series , featuring three all-Original Six matchups in three days. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Blueshirts’ history began on Nov. 16, 1926, when they hosted the Montreal Maroons, the defending Stanley Cup champions. The Rangers announced their arrival in style, blanking the Maroons 1-0 in front of an estimated crowd of 13,000. Bill Cook scored the franchise’s first goal at 18:37 of the second period, and it held up as the winner. Goaltender Hal Winkler was the star of the night, turning away all 48 shots he faced to secure the shutout. That game was played at the third version of Madison Square Garden, located about a mile north of the team’s current home. The Rangers went on to win the Stanley Cup in just their second season, in 1928. A century later, the Rangers are once again facing a team from Montreal. The Canadiens came into the night with a 12-4-4 record, while New York entered at 12-8-1. Adam Fox has led the way for the Rangers this season with a team-high 23 points, including 21 assists. Interestingly, the Canadiens were without former Rangers forward Chris Kreider , who is sidelined for six to eight weeks with an injury. The Rangers will look to cap off their historic night at the Garden with a fitting win over their Original Six rivals. item.title: Red Sox Making Very Smart Decision With Willson Contreras After Jake Bauers Deal
item.description: Red Sox Making Very Smart Decision With Willson Contreras After Jake Bauers Deal originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . When it was announced that the Boston Red Sox planned to sign Jake Bauers to a four-year deal, questions immediately arose about whether Willson Contreras would be moved or lose some of his at-bats. However, given that he was among the best hitters in the Red Sox's lineup a year ago, if not the best, it wouldn't have made much sense for Boston to go either way. That's why the latest report, which should have Red Sox fans very happy, should clear things up about what the organization plans to do. This wasn't to replace Contreras, but more so just to add another really good bat to the lineup on top of what Contreras can do. “That list brings up a good question: What happens to Contreras now? He led the team in home runs (27) and RBIs (81) last year, and was second (4.0) behind Ceddanne Rafaela (4.1) in fWAR. Actually, that’s an easy answer: He and Bauers are likely to split time between first base and DH,” Ken Rosenthal wrote . As long as both guys are in the lineup, there shouldn't be too much of an issue here for the Red Sox. President of baseball operations Craig Breslow entered the offseason with an obvious need to improve on the offensive side of the baseball. He spoke about it many times, saying his biggest focus was that he needed to find some external candidates who could come in and help this offense. Bauers was arguably the most important piece to the Milwaukee Brewers' playoff run and has a real opportunity to do some damage in Boston with a short right-field porch. item.title: ‘Josh Allen is NOT a top 3 MVP candidate’: Ryan Clark takes a stand
item.description: Jan 11, 2026; Jacksonville, FL, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) warms up before an AFC Wild Card Round game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images The Buffalo Bills are rolling, improving to 8-1 on the season with a 31-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday. And as usual, quarterback Josh Allen is right in the middle of the MVP conversation. But former NFL safety Ryan Clark isn’t buying it. On Monday, Clark made it clear that he doesn’t think Allen belongs among the top three MVP candidates, and he took particular issue with how Allen’s touchdown totals are being used to build his case. Allen’s MVP Case Allen, who won MVP in 2024, has been his usual productive self in 2026. Through nine games, he has thrown for 2,223 yards with 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions, while adding 11 rushing touchdowns. The rushing touchdowns have been a big part of his MVP case, with Allen racking up 24 total touchdowns so far. And the Bills own the best record in the AFC after winning their fifth straight game on Sunday. But some other quarterbacks have put together big seasons, too. Joe Burrow, who has drawn plenty of praise this season, threw for 409 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals’ 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night, as the Bengals improved to 7-2. Brock Purdy threw for 389 yards in the San Francisco 49ers’ 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys, and the 49ers are now 8-1. Trevor Lawrence also had a big afternoon, throwing for 352 yards in the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans to improve to 7-2. ‘Not a Top 3 MVP Candidate’ With all that elite play from the quarterback position this year, Clark made his MVP picks on Monday, and Allen didn’t make the cut. “Josh Allen is NOT a top 3 MVP candidate! Joe Burrow. Brock Purdy. Trevor Lawrence. That’s my 3! Love Josh, but we can’t confuse who he IS with how he’s PLAYING!” Clark wrote on X . Clark also took a shot at the way Allen’s rushing touchdowns have been used to boost his MVP case. “And enough with the total TD graphics! We KNOW he has 8 QB sneak TDs. They count, and they take toughness & skill, but they aren’t equivalent to what Joe, Brock & Trevor are doing! All TDs count. They don’t all tell the same MVP story!” Clark wrote. Clark has never been one to shy away from strong takes, and this one drew plenty of pushback from Bills fans in the replies. Even so, his point about Allen’s passing numbers is hard to ignore, as Allen’s 2,223 passing yards rank just 14th in the NFL. Needless to say, Bills fans probably won’t be changing their minds anytime soon. The post ‘Josh Allen is NOT a top 3 MVP candidate’: Ryan Clark takes a stand appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Everything Dan Lanning said before Oregon visits Michigan State
item.description: The job remains unfinished for Dan Lanning . After stringing together three straight wins and thrusting themselves back into the playoff conversation, the Oregon Ducks will tackle another bit of adversity this week: a short turnaround for a conference road game against the Michigan State Spartans . Oregon avoided a letdown last week with a dominant 31-7 victory over Michigan, in which Dylan Raiola tossed four touchdowns, and both Dakorien Moore and Jeremiah McClellan exceeded 100 receiving yards. The offense is clicking at the right time, and the Ducks ' defense continued its strong second half, forcing two more turnovers. Now, Lanning will lead the Ducks back out on the road, this time to East Lansing, where the Spartans have struggled this season, but are playing better as of late. A night tilt on the road in an environment hoping to play spoiler should put a target on Oregon's back, especially as the national expectations continue to rise. Lanning opened up on the success of the offense in recent weeks, as well as other storylines for the win over Michigan, and previewed the upcoming matchup with the Spartans at his weekly press conference. Here's everything Lanning had to say before Oregon takes on Michigan State on Friday night. Opening Statement Dan Lanning: "It was an awesome atmosphere at Autzen, but really not a lot of time to think about that game. A quick turnaround for us as a coaching staff because we have a short week this week. So we really were able to put the Michigan game to bed pretty quickly and get a jump. Kind of treated Sunday in a lot of ways like a Monday from a prep standpoint for us as a coaching staff, and really hit the ground running today with practice. Have to modify the look a little bit of what that'll look like in a week that's short. So today was more of a Tuesday for our players from a prep standpoint, and then tomorrow will be a little bit more of a Wednesday/Tuesday combined as we continue throughout the week. But some good prep; proud of some of the performance that our guys were able to have on Saturday, and certainly still some things that we can get better at. But as you prep for this Michigan State team, you see a team that's getting better and better. They've dealt with some injuries like everybody is at this point in the season, but coach Fitzgerald does an unbelievable job. You can see the toughness going out with his group, and the pride that they play with and how hard they play. Certainly gives us a unique challenge traveling to a place that we actually haven't yet experienced in East Lansing. So, it should be a fun environment Friday night, and we're excited about that opportunity." Evan Stewart Question: You had a long talk with Evan after the second quarter, going into halftime. I don't think he played in the second half either. What was the reasoning for that? DL: "Yeah, I won't get into details. I'll just say that football is, in a lot of ways, like a family. You'll have disagreements at time

Have to modify the look a little bit of what that'll look like in a week that's short. So today was more of a Tuesday for our players from a prep standpoint, and then tomorrow will be a little bit more of a Wednesday/Tuesday combined as we continue throughout the week. But some good prep; proud of some of the performance that our guys were able to have on Saturday, and certainly still some things that we can get better at. But as you prep for this Michigan State team, you see a team that's getting better and better. They've dealt with some injuries like everybody is at this point in the season, but coach Fitzgerald does an unbelievable job. You can see the toughness going out with his group, and the pride that they play with and how hard they play. Certainly gives us a unique challenge traveling to a place that we actually haven't yet experienced in East Lansing. So, it should be a fun environment Friday night, and we're excited about that opportunity." Evan Stewart Question: You had a long talk with Evan after the second quarter, going into halftime. I don't think he played in the second half either. What was the reasoning for that? DL: "Yeah, I won't get into details. I'll just say that football is, in a lot of ways, like a family. You'll have disagreements at times. He's a passionate player. I'm a passionate coach, and we'll keep that really within us. But I know how much he wants to do a good job for this team, for himself personally, and I have expectations that he can create that moving forward." Q: To clarify, he'll be available this upcoming game? DL: "Yeah." Fourth Down Defense Q: I just want to ask you about fourth down defense. I think you guys are 8-of-12 allowing opponents coming into these last two games and have held the last seven without conversions. Can you speak to whether it's a law of averages, or you're bound to get more stops? Has there been something you've seen from a growth perspective? DL: "Yeah, I mean it's a combination. We've certainly put a lot of emphasis on it and worked at it. I think as coaches, you instinctively start to really focus on attacking things when you get to third down. The most exotic stuff and the funnest stuff. And fourth down is no different to run. It's on fourth-and-long, right? On third-and-long, you've got some really cool answers, some really cool things that you can do. The reality is, what situations are going to show up more often? What do you need to be prepared for more? What's harder? It's short yardage. It's fourth-and-one. It's fourth-and-two. So I think as a staff, we really challenge ourselves to make sure we have really good answers there. Make sure that our players have a lot of confidence to operate in those moments and create a lot of those in practice, rather than some of the exotic looks that you might get on longer D-and-Ds. And the transverse of that is offense, right? You want to have a great repertoire of things that you can do in short yardage, right? Because those moments are going to show up, but you come with a lot of cool things at third-and-three to six. But the reality is, what are you going to do when it's long, right? I think we've seen both of those really have an uptick for our team because we focused on making it a little bit harder for our offense in practice, and making it a little bit harder for our defense in practice with some of the situations that we practiced, and then our players just executing those moments well. But as you saw with the Dierre touchdown in the game, and you saw it against Ohio State where we were able to convert some third-and-longs with some unique prep and some different looks. I think all those things have shown up for us." Titan's Championship Q: Your son's championship game on Saturday. What was that experience like for you after obviously playing your own game? What was the situation with the lights? Had (Oregon State coach) Shepard helped out with that, or what was the deal? DL: "It was funny to go see those guys play. I had some memories being in that stadium because we didn't do well at one time I was there, and it looks a lot different now. They've done a good job with the construction, but I was kind of reliving some of those moments. But getting to watch Titan play was a blast. I guess there had been several games there throughout the night, and it was supposed to be done at 10 p.m. The game was, for whatever reason, going a little bit long. It's 12-6, and it's 10:05 p.m., and boom, all the lights shut off. The game's not over. There's two minutes and 30 seconds left. So, somebody comes out on the announcement, and Titan's team is ahead, and they say, 'Oh, that's the game.' And obviously, if you're on the other team, you're not going to be excited about that result. Right across the street are their practice fields, and the lights were still on there, so I think the young guys were saying, 'Hey, fine, let's just go finish it over there on those fields.' So we went across the street, and it was kind of like 'The Legend of Bagger Vance,' man. We had all the parents all around, and we played the last two minutes and 30 seconds of that game. So it was a lot of fun to get to watch him. But I got to see him play. Every one of his games this year, so getting to see that one was a lot of fun, and it was fun after riding back with him in the car talking about it." Bear Alexander Q: Bear shared a pretty gnarly picture of his twisted ankle or something that happened to whatever his lower body. DL: "Did you think it's AI? Do you think it's a real picture?" Q: Pretty gnarly looking. DL: "Yeah, tough kid." Q: How do you manage the wear and tear of that? Is there a snap count, or how do you manage it? DL: "He got rolled up on his unique play, and he's a tough guy. I mean, that's one of those ones where I think it speaks to him going in, getting taped up, and saying, 'I want to get back in the game, and again, at this point in the year, there's a lot of guys that have rolled ankles, but that was a pretty significant one. You limit him at the beginning of the week, you see what he's able to do, and obviously we want to put him out there with his best foot forward. But I think it speaks to his toughness. I think the fumble that he created

item.title: Jets reportedly received ‘bad’ intel on Liam Coen before hiring Aaron Glenn
item.description: Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images The New York Jets reportedly received misleading information about Liam Coen during their search for a head coach, which helped steer the franchise towards hiring Aaron Glenn instead. The revelation has raised fresh questions about the decision-making behind Glenn’s appointment. According to the New York Post’s Brian Costello, the Jets carried out their research on Coen but were given a negative assessment of his suitability for the role. That decision looks particularly costly now, with Coen enjoying an impressive start to life as Jacksonville Jaguars head coach while Glenn continues to struggle in New York. Mike Tannenbaum reportedly among those who advised against Liam Coen Speaking on Gang’s All Here , Costello explained how the Jets were reportedly discouraged from pursuing Coen. “What happened with Liam Coen with the Jets is I was told they got bad information,” Costello said. He added: “They were told that he wasn’t a good fit; they were told he might not be a good head coach. They were like–they did their due diligence on Liam Coen like they did on everybody. And the scouting report, so to speak, that they got a Liam Coen has turned out to be completely incorrect. They were talking to the wrong people.” Costello indicated that the group providing the information included former Jets general manager Mike Tannenbaum, who now works as an analyst for ESPN. Coen has since guided Jacksonville to a 7-2 record and the top spot in the AFC South. The Jaguars are also the third seed in the AFC, with Coen having made an impressive start to his head coaching career. Glenn, meanwhile, has a 5-22 record since taking charge of the Jets. New York sit just one win above the bottom-placed Miami Dolphins. The situation has also brought renewed scrutiny of Glenn’s leadership. After spending four seasons as Detroit Lions defensive coordinator, he was expected to take a more CEO-like approach in New York, but his coaching appointments have also come under criticism. The Jets have a decision to make about Glenn’s future, with general manager Darren Mougey and owner Woody Johnson ultimately responsible for determining whether he remains in charge beyond this season. item.title: Brewers Betting on Rebound Season From Former Stud Reliever
item.description: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - JULY 01: Manager Tony Vitello #23 gestures towards the bullpen as relief pitcher Ryan Walker #74 of the San Francisco Giants walks off the field during a pitching change in the eighth inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on July 01, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) Getty On Sunday, the World Series Champion Milwaukee Brewers added a reliever to their staff. That reliever was Ryan Walker, whom they got from the San Francisco Giants. To get him, they traded two prospects, Blake Holub and Gavin Perry. We have acquired RHP Ryan Walker from SF in exchange for Minor Leaguers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry Welcome, Ryan! pic.twitter.com/lzVJwofNHj — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) November 15, 2026 The Brewers are making a calculated bet here: Has Walker lost his effectiveness, or does he simply need the right opportunity to get back on track? Walker is coming off a very poor 2026 season. But the Brewers are betting they can help him return to his old self, not the player everyone saw in 2026. Will Walker Be Better With the Brewers? Before his poor last season, Walker was a strong bullpen arm for three seasons. Fans responded quickly once they heard the news. “Omg he’s gonna turn into a demon now,” said one fan. “They will turn Walker into the best closer in baseball next year,” wrote another. Walker already showed what he can do. He made his major league debut in 2023, and between 2023 and 2025, his ERA was a very good 2.98. His WHIP was 1.140. He pitched 202.2 innings, recorded 28 saves, racked up 237 strikeouts, and allowed only 60 walks. He had established himself as an elite reliever who could do more than eat innings. He was entrusted with crucial situations. What Went Wrong in 2026? Things slipped for Walker last season. His earned run average jumped to a whopping 7.16. His WHIP was 1.806. He pitched only 32.2 innings, with 23 strikeouts and 19 walks. It got so bad that he was demoted to Triple-A three times. That’s a significant drop from his previous performance. His control became a problem, and he walked nearly as many batters as he struck out. The Giants sent him to Triple-A three times. No one knows exactly what caused the decline, but it was certainly evident. Milwaukee Didn’t Empty Their Cupboard to Get Walker The Brewers gave up very little to acquire Walker, making it a fairly risk-free trade. Blake Holub was a 15th-round pick by Detroit in 2021. He came to Milwaukee in the trade for Mark Canha. He pitched in Triple-A Nashville and posted a 2.10 ERA with a 1.257 WHIP. He pitched 55 and 2/3 innings, with 66 strikeouts and 21 walks. He has a mid-90s cutter and a mid-80s slider. Gavin Perry was an 11th-round pick in 2026 from Western Kentucky. He put up 85 2/3 innings, allowing 19 walks and four home runs. Both have potential, but neither has established himself in the major leagues. He’s already shown major-league success, and they believe they can bring him back from ineffective to elite. If this is to work, the Brewers need better command and consistency. If he can return to his form from the past three seasons before 2026, he could become a huge bullpen addition for the team. If not, Milwaukee hasn’t given up much. The bottom line is that the Brewers are giving Walker a fresh chance, and he has something to prove. The question is, can he do it? item.title: Clark-Willow Lake sophomore Shelby Begeman leads All-NEC volleyball team
item.description: Area high school volleyball players have been honored by being selected for all-conference honors in the Northeast Conference and 281 Conference. Here are the honorees: All-Northeast Conference Clark-Willow Lake sophomore Shelby Begeman earned Offensive and Defensive Player of the Year honors and is one of four All-NEC players for the conference champion Cyclones. CWL went 10-0 in league play. Begeman earned repeat all-conference honors and is joined on the squad by teammates Kelsey Hofer, a senior; Ella Sass and Kamryn Nesheim, each juniors. Sass also earned repeat all-league honors. 2025 All-NEC VOLLEYBALL: Area volleyball and football players receive year-end honors in three area conferences Three-time selections Issie Steffensen of Hamlin and Mallory Steiner of Webster Area also made the team along with other repeat honorees Elyana Roach of Aberdeen Roncalli and Jaelee Grupe of Britton-Hecla, both juniors. Rounding out the squad are junior Jillian Ellwein and sophomore Grace Cogley of Aberdeen Roncalli, freshman Lauryn Peterreins of Deuel, junior Addie Jensen of Hamlin, senior Charli Jungwirth of Redfield and senior Taryn Traphagen, junior Sydney Locke and sophomore Tevan Hanson of Groton Area. All-281 Conference Four players from conference champion Wolsey-Wessington spearhead the squad, including first-team selections Shae Uttecht, Maria Nelson and Preslie Jensen. item.title: Los Angeles Rams Announce Bad News for Matthew Stafford
item.description: Matthew Stafford and the Rams got more bad news on the injury front. Getty The hits keep coming for Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams, with the latest being the loss of starting center and Super Bowl champion Coleman Shelton. “Rams center Coleman Shelton suffered a hamstring strain and is expected to miss 4-6 weeks, per team spokesperson,” the LA Daily News’ Adam Grosbard reported in a post on X on November 16. Others soon corroborated the report. Rams center Coleman Shelton suffered a hamstring strain against Cardinals and will be out 4 to 6 weeks, a team official said. — Gary Klein (@LATimesklein) November 17, 2026 This news comes after the Rams placed Shelton’s replacement, Dylan McMahon on injured reserve. McMahon must miss at least four games. Rams Lose Super Bowl Champion Coleman Shelton to Hamstring Injury The Rams are on their bye in Week 11. That means that McMahon will now be sidelined at least until Week 16. Moreover, Shelton will be out anywhere from Week 15 through Week 17 after suffering his injury in Week 10 against the Arizona Cardinals. LA was also without starting right guard Steve Avila and backup Justin Dedich. As it stands, their remaining interior options are Beau Limmer, Bill Murray, and David Quessenberry, who is a tackle. Limmer was the Rams’ starting center during the 2024 season. This is the latest setback on the injury front. LA is without starting wide receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, tight end Terrance Ferguson, defensive back Jaylen Watson, and defensive linemen Kobie Turner and Poona Ford (who is out for the season). Shelton, 31, was an undrafted free agent. He was a member of the 2021 Super Bowl team. He spent one year with the Chicago Bears after signing as a free agent in 2024. Shelton returned to LA in the same fashion in 2025. He has started 59 of his 100 games with the Rams. Stafford has called Shelton a “vital” part of what the team wants to do as an offense. The QB cited the center’s communication even in hostile environments during games. That is what the Rams will miss the most. “He’s vital. He’s vital. His ability to communicate, in loud environments, what we want to get done quickly, concisely, and clearly for all those guys up front was integral in how well we played both in the run game and the pass game,” Stafford told reporters in August. “Setting the fronts quickly. ‘Here we go. Let’s push the tempo’ and the only way you can do that is if everybody’s aligned up front. “He does such a great job of communicating and spreading that word down the line of scrimmage for those guys, so they can play with a quiet mind and play fast and physical.” The Rams have two road games over the projected timeline for Shelton’s return. However, they are against the Rams’ top competition in the NFC West, the division-leading San Francisco 49ers and the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. item.title: Fantasy Football Week 11 Injury Report: Drake Maye, Brock Bowers And More
item.description: Drake Maye of the New England Patriots might be done for the season due to an ankle injury. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty Images Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season was pure carnage for fantasy football managers from an injury standpoint. Week 10 largely provided a much-needed reprieve. A pair of New England Patriots suffered injuries that could jeopardize their availability moving forward, but they’re heading into a bye in Week 11, so they weren’t going to be in fantasy lineups next week either way. Aside from that, only one other early-round fantasy pick went down with an in-game injury, although another second-rounder missed Week 10 after a late-week downgrade. Every week, we’ll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup moving forward. Let’s dive into all of the most notable updates ahead of Week 10. Patriots QB Drake Maye (ankle) The NFL thought it was getting Drake Maye vs. Jared Goff in Munich, Germany. Instead, it got Goff vs. Tommy DeVito for most of the game. Maye guided the New England Patriots on an 11-play, 60-yard drive on their opening drive, but he suffered an ankle injury while getting sacked on 3rd-and-goal and did not return. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Patriots “are concerned” that Maye fractured his ankle, which could be a season-ending injury. The NFL trade deadline just passed, so it seems as though DeVito will be starting for the Patriots upon their return from bye in Week 12 and beyond. DeVito should be better prepared for that start than he was on Sunday, but losing Maye is a major downgrade to all Patriots skill-position players. Patriots WR A.J. Brown (hamstring) On the bright side, A.J. Brown might not have to worry about the loss of Maye. That’s because his nightmare season continued Sunday when he suffered a hamstring injury on a 21-yard reception late in the third quarter. Including Sunday’s loss, Brown has played in only four games during his debut campaign with the Patriots. He suffered a high ankle sprain in the season opener that sidelined him for four weeks, missed Weeks 8 and 9 with knee and ankle injuries, then returned Sunday only to suffer another injury. Given the downgrade from Maye to DeVito, owners in 10-team leagues should seriously consider dropping Brown, particularly with the Patriots on bye in Week 11. Barring a drastic late-season turnaround, he’ll be going down as one of the biggest early-round busts of the year. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (ankle) Brock Bowers figured to be the first, second and third option for Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in his first regular-season start. However, that plan went awry less than five minutes into their game against the Seattle Seahawks when he suffered an ankle injury on a 3rd-and-3 run play on the Raiders’ first drive. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty Images Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season was pure carnage for fantasy football managers from an injury standpoint. Every week, we’ll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup moving forward. Let’s dive into all of the most notable updates ahead of Week 10. Patriots QB Drake Maye (ankle) The NFL thought it was getting Drake Maye vs. Jared Goff in Munich, Germany. Instead, it got Goff vs. Tommy DeVito for most of the game. Maye guided the New England Patriots on an 11-play, 60-yard drive on their opening drive, but he suffered an ankle injury while getting sacked on 3rd-and-goal and did not return. The NFL trade deadline just passed, so it seems as though DeVito will be starting for the Patriots upon their return from bye in Week 12 and beyond. DeVito should be better prepared for that start than he was on Sunday, but losing Maye is a major downgrade to all Patriots skill-position players. Patriots WR A.J. Brown (hamstring) On the bright side, A.J. Brown might not have to worry about the loss of Maye. That’s because his nightmare season continued Sunday when he suffered a hamstring injury on a 21-yard reception late in the third quarter. Including Sunday’s loss, Brown has played in only four games during his debut campaign with the Patriots. He suffered a high ankle sprain in the season opener that sidelined him for four weeks, missed Weeks 8 and 9 with knee and ankle injuries, then returned Sunday only to suffer another injury. Given the downgrade from Maye to DeVito, owners in 10-team leagues should seriously consider dropping Brown, particularly with the Patriots on bye in Week 11. Barring a drastic late-season turnaround, he’ll be going down as one of the biggest early-round busts of the year. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (ankle) Brock Bowers figured to be the first, second and third option for Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in his first regular-season start. However, that plan went awry less than five minutes into their game against the Seattle Seahawks when he suffered an ankle injury on a 3rd-and-3 run play on the Raiders’ first drive. Bowers briefly returned to the game on two separate occasions, but he eventually went back to the locker room and was ruled out. Luckily for fantasy managers, he “is not believed to have suffered a major ankle injury,” according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , and “is considered day-to-day.” Mendoza finished 17-of-29 for 143 yards against the Seahawks while getting sacked six times. He’s bound to go through growing pains as he acclimates to the NFL, which might reduce Bowers’ ceiling. Then again, Mendoza might be more prone than a veteran to lock on to his first target, which will typically be Bowers. Fantasy managers should thus expect more variance in Bowers’ rest-of-season outlook whenever he does return. Vikings WR Jordan Addison (thumb) Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison wasn’t even listed on his team’s injury report on Wednesday or Thursday last week. However, he got in a limited practice Friday because of a thumb injury and was eventually ruled out before the game began. On Monday, fantasy managers finally gained more clarity into what happened: The Vikings offense looked better with trade-deadline acquisition Kirk Cousins at the helm, as Justin Jefferson hauled in a season-high nine catches on 13 targets for 74 yards. Both Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson were sidelined, which reduced his competition for targets, but his rest-of-season outlook is now pointing straight up, especially with Addison out for the next few weeks. Myles Price, who caught four passes for 46 yards and a touchdown in Addison’s absence, should be a priority target on waivers this week. Texans RB Woody Marks (concussion) Houston Texans running back David Montgomery missed his fourth straight game with a groin injury, which once again cleared the way for Woody Marks to run wild as the team’s RB1. However, Marks suffered a concussion in the third quarter and did not return, which left the Texans down to Emari Demarcado and Dare Ogunbowale at running back. After the game, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters that he doesn’t expect Marks to clear the concussion protocol in time for his team’s Week 11 game against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night. He added that he was “not certain” if Montgomery would be back even though Montgomery got in a limited practice Thursday and a full practice Friday this past week. Even if Montgomery is able to return, he might not get a full workload, particularly since the Texans are overwhelming favorites against the playing-out-the-string Colts. If he can’t go, Demarcado and Ogunbowale could be worth a look for desperate managers who’ve been besieged by injuries and/or bye weeks. Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith had a tough day against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. He missed the first drive after halftime because he was undergoing a concussion evaluation. Upon his return, he then suffered an ankle injury later in the third quarter that knocked him out for the day. On Monday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that Smith is undergoing tests on his ankle, but that he’d remain the Jets’ starter in Week 11 against the Los Angeles Chargers if healthy. Fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik replaced Smith for most of the second half against the Bills and finished 11-of-20 with 137 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception. The 0-8 Chargers could provide the beleaguered Jets offense with a get-right spot regardless of whether Smith or Klubnik starts. Garrett Wilson, who finished with a team-high seven catches for 106 yards against the Bills, figures to be busy either way. Quick Hits Jets WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle): Cooper left early in Sunday’s game with an ankle injury and is undergoing tests to determine the severity of it. Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and running back Breece Hall should all be in line for more targets moving forward until he’s able to return. Seahawks RB George Holani (knee): Holani suffered an MCL sprain against the Raiders and is considered week-to-week, according to Rapoport . With both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price now back in the fold, Holani doesn’t belong on any fantasy rosters, particularly in the wake of this injury. Returning Soon? Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III (groin) Kenneth Walker III was a surprise addition to the Kansas City Chiefs’ injury report with a groin injury on Friday, and they wound up ruling him out on Saturday. Sources told Schefter and Rapoport that the injury is minor, but “because it occurred in practice Thursday, it made it a tough turnaround for Walker.” During an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Monday , Schefter said the Chiefs “believe it’s a short-term injury.” However, he added that he wouldn’t be surprised if Walker missed Week 11, particularly since backup running back Emmett Johnson has been playing well. Either way, Walker should be back in fantasy lineups soon. But if you have him on your roster and don’t have Johnson as a handcuff, you should spend the early part of this week getting a backup plan ready just in case. item.title: Ravens hit historic low with brutal rushing stat vs. Chargers
item.description: Mandatory Credit: James Lang-Imagn Images Ravens hit historic low with brutal rushing stat vs. Chargers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens made unwanted history in the first half of their showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. The Ravens found themselves trailing the visiting Los Angeles side after the first half, 17-10. Although Baltimore scored a rushing touchdown courtesy of star running back and future Pro Football Hall of Famer Derrick Henry in the second quarter, the Ravens still finished the first half with a net total of zero yards on the ground, a brutal low the franchise had not hit ever before. “The Ravens rushed for 0 yards in the 1st half, their fewest in a 1st half in franchise history. They had 6 handoffs in the 1st half and were hit at or behind the line on 5 of those rushes,” ESPN Insights shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Ravens entered the game looking to rely more once again on the abilities of Henry and the team’s rushing attack with Lamar Jackson out and Jacoby Brissett making his first-ever appearance under center for Baltimore. Over the first nine weeks of the season, Baltimore ranked fifth overall in the league with an average of 137.8 rushing yards per game, which makes the team’s struggles on the ground in the first half of the meeting with the Chargers even more befuddling. The Ravens are trying to keep their playoff hopes alive, as they have slid all the way down to the bottom of the AFC North standings with a 4-5 record through nine weeks. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty Kevon Looney #55 of the Los Angeles Lakers Getty The Los Angeles Lakers will be without Walker Kessler when they return home Tuesday against the Charlotte Hornets, leaving coach JJ Redick with a difficult decision at center. Kessler was ruled out because of right lower leg soreness, according to the NBA’s injury report released Monday. The designation comes one day after Kessler recorded 14 points, 12 rebounds and two blocks in Los Angeles’ 131-123 victory over the Phoenix Suns. The 25-year-old center made four of five shots and all six of his free throws while finishing with a plus-18 rating. Now, the Lakers must replace his interior presence as they attempt to extend their eight-game winning streak. Walker Kessler Injury Leaves Lakers With Frontcourt Question Getty Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers blocks a shot by Draymond Green of the Golden State Warriors during the second half of a game at Crypto.com Arena on October 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Kessler has been one of Los Angeles’ most dependable frontcourt players this season. Through 14 games, he is averaging approximately 14.5 points and 10.9 rebounds while providing the rim protection the Lakers desperately need. His impact extends beyond those numbers. Kessler gives Luka Doncic a reliable target around the basket, creates second-chance opportunities and helps protect a defense that has struggled despite the team’s impressive record. Los Angeles entered Monday at 12-2, tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the NBA’s best record. However, the Lakers rank just 17th in defensive efficiency, allowing 114 points per 100 possessions. Without Kessler, Redick faces an unfamiliar frontcourt challenge. Veteran Kevon Looney appears to be a logical replacement, but his limited playing time raises questions about how much the Lakers can expect from him. Kevon Looney Has Barely Played Since October Getty Kevon Looney of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket against Charles Bassey of the Golden State Warriors in the third quarter of a preseason game at T-Mobile Are

(Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty Kevon Looney #55 of the Los Angeles Lakers Getty The Los Angeles Lakers will be without Walker Kessler when they return home Tuesday against the Charlotte Hornets, leaving coach JJ Redick with a difficult decision at center. Kessler was ruled out because of right lower leg soreness, according to the NBA’s injury report released Monday. The designation comes one day after Kessler recorded 14 points, 12 rebounds and two blocks in Los Angeles’ 131-123 victory over the Phoenix Suns. The 25-year-old center made four of five shots and all six of his free throws while finishing with a plus-18 rating. Now, the Lakers must replace his interior presence as they attempt to extend their eight-game winning streak. Walker Kessler Injury Leaves Lakers With Frontcourt Question Getty Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers blocks a shot by Draymond Green of the Golden State Warriors during the second half of a game at Crypto.com Arena on October 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Kessler has been one of Los Angeles’ most dependable frontcourt players this season. Through 14 games, he is averaging approximately 14.5 points and 10.9 rebounds while providing the rim protection the Lakers desperately need. His impact extends beyond those numbers. Kessler gives Luka Doncic a reliable target around the basket, creates second-chance opportunities and helps protect a defense that has struggled despite the team’s impressive record. Los Angeles entered Monday at 12-2, tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the NBA’s best record. However, the Lakers rank just 17th in defensive efficiency, allowing 114 points per 100 possessions. Without Kessler, Redick faces an unfamiliar frontcourt challenge. Veteran Kevon Looney appears to be a logical replacement, but his limited playing time raises questions about how much the Lakers can expect from him. Kevon Looney Has Barely Played Since October Getty Kevon Looney of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket against Charles Bassey of the Golden State Warriors in the third quarter of a preseason game at T-Mobile Arena on October 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Warriors defeated the Lakers 101-89. Looney has fallen out of Redick’s regular rotation. Since playing five minutes against Portland on Oct. 27, the veteran center has logged just four minutes of actual playing time, coming against Milwaukee on Nov. 11. He recorded two rebounds without attempting a shot. The 30-year-old provides championship experience, rebounding and physicality. However, his lack of recent playing time could complicate an expanded assignment. Redick could alternatively turn to Sandro Mamukelashvili, whose shooting and passing offer a different look at center. Smaller lineups are another possibility. The decision comes after Los Angeles nearly squandered a 31-point lead against Phoenix. The Suns scored 43 fourth-quarter points, exposing defensive lapses that Redick has repeatedly criticized. “You have to play for 48 minutes,” Redick said afterward. The Lakers coach emphasized that his team must maintain its defensive intensity regardless of the scoreboard. Kessler’s absence could make that task considerably harder. Charlotte will also be shorthanded, with Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder ruled out because of hamstring injuries. Still, Los Angeles must find a way to control the paint without its starting center. Kessler’s return timeline remains uncertain. Until then, Redick may have to trust a veteran who has spent most of the past three weeks watching from the bench. item.title: Lakers’ Austin Reaves Remains Out as Walker Kessler Joins Injury List vs. Hornets
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Lakers ruled out Walker Kessler and Austin Reaves for Tuesday, Nov. 17th clash against the Charlotte Hornets. Austin Reaves’ injury outlook Reaves missed Sunday’s game against the Phoenix Suns after suffering a heel injury last week against the Milwaukee Bucks. Even after three full days of rest, Reaves was not ready to play against the Suns, and now, almost a week later, he is still out. The X-rays on his heel came back clean, meaning there is no structural damage to his foot, and it is labeled as a bruise. Overall, when speaking to the media, head coach JJ Redick does not seem too concerned. “He’s improving,” Redick said. “It really comes down to just like a pain tolerance thing. Again, nothing structural beyond a bruise. And so I think every day it’s been better, and we’ll see where he’s at in 48 hours when we play on Tuesday. The Lakers have a back-to-back coming up, with the Hornets game followed by another home game against the Utah Jazz. Perhaps LA is holding him out until Wednesday’s game, though they may wait until Friday, Nov. 20th against the Sacramento Kings. The Jazz, Hornets, and Kings are among the worst teams in the league, and the Lakers may rest Reaves for much of this stretch. Why Kessler will be sorely missed Meanwhile, on the big-man front, Walker Kessler is out on Tuesday for the first time this year. He appeared on the injury report with right lower leg soreness. Without Kessler, things will get quite hairy for the Lakers on the big-man front. Kevon Looney, the veteran center, may get the start, though he has struggled this year and has been a defensive liability due to his lack of mobility. Overall, Looney is a plodding big man who offers nowhere near the rim protection and movement that Kessler does as both a lob threat and shot-alterer. Nov 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) reaches for the ball against Milwaukee Bucks forward Jaime Jaquez Jr. (24) and center Kel’el Ware (9) in the fourth quarter at Fiserv Forum. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The other option will be Carson Cooper, who is on a two-way contract. If the Lakers want to play some small-ball and move away from their size options, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jared Vanderbilt can play center. Their lack of size costs the team on the boards, but they are strong enough to hold their own against other centers in limited stretches. No matter which path they start with, it will end up looking like a mix of both approaches. The post Lakers’ Austin Reaves Remains Out as Walker Kessler Joins Injury List vs. Hornets appeared first on LA Sports Report .

item.title: Patriots' AJ Brown Trade Considered 'Laughable' as Injuries and Struggles Continue
item.description: Patriots' AJ Brown Trade Considered 'Laughable' as Injuries and Struggles Continue originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's almost tough to justify the New England Patriots making that trade for A.J. Brown now. The hope was that Brown would be among the best wide receivers in the NFL, similar to what he's been throughout much of his career. Unfortunately, after the Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder for the disgruntled star with the Philadelphia Eagles at the time, nothing has gone as planned. Whether it's because Brown has been dealing with injuries or because he isn't the same wide receiver he once was, it's obvious this trade hasn't been a positive one for New England. This season, Brown has just 11 receptions for 428 yards. There hasn't been a game yet where he looks even decent, or like the shell of himself he was in Philadelphia. As for how some fans and writers feel about the situation in New England, the frustration is at an all-time high. When recently examining the situation, one writer went as far as to say that the inability to do anything positive this year has almost been funny. “The A.J. Brown trade keeps looking worse by the day. A.J. Brown’s inability to do anything positive this year has been almost laughable. He got hurt in the first game, missed a good chunk of time on injured reserve, came back, was a non-factor, and then got hurt again. He returned on Sunday, was unable to get open and had a drop as well. “He finally made a nice catch-and-run to move the stick on a third down, and then promptly went to the locker room with a hamstring injury. It’s been a rough year for Brown, and the Patriots front office: they effectively bid against themselves to trade for him and still gave up a first-round pick in 2028 to do so. Unless he somehow manages a complete 180, the trade is going to go down as a massive failure, and potentially hamstring the Patriots for years to come,” Pat Lane wrote . It really doesn't make much sense that Brown is playing at this level, unless that injury is as bad as it could be. The reality is that if he’s still dealing with that injury, we're not going to see the same type of player we're used to seeing. However, Brown just hasn't been able to do anything on the offensive side of the football and looks like he’s lost a ton of burst. I'm not ready to say this is one of the worst trades the Patriots have made in a long time, but if it doesn't change soon, it'll be tough to say otherwise. More Patriots news: Three Things Patriots Must Fix Following Drake Maye Injury Can Tommy DeVito Keep Patriots’ Season Alive Without Drake Maye Mike Vrabel Makes Feelings Clear About Aidan Hutchinson’s Hit on Drake Maye

item.title: New York Yankees Interested in 3-Time All-Star Free Agent Outfielder
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 01: Randy Arozarena #56 of the Seattle Mariners looks on during the first inning against the Minnesota Twins at T-Mobile Park on August 01, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) Getty LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 10: General Manager Brian Cashman of the New York Yankees speaks with the media during the 2026 MLB Gerneral Managers Meetings at Aria Resort & Casino on November 10, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 27: Randy Arozarena #56 of the Seattle Mariners lifts his hat as he runs in from the outfield after being pulled from the game during the seventh inning against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 27, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Getty The New York Yankees have “checked in” on three-time All-Star free agent outfielder Randy Arozarena, according to The New York Post’s Jon Heyman. The Yankees don’t really need a corner outfielder, but the Yankees appear to be interested regardless. If New York ends up signing Arozarena, the team could move 2026 Platinum Glove Award winner Cody Bellinger to center field. Bellinger mainly played left field this past season. New York Yankees “Checked in” on Randy Arozarena Getty LAS VEGAS, NEVADA – NOVEMBER 10: General Manager Brian Cashman of the New York Yankees speaks with the media during the 2026 MLB Gerneral Managers Meetings at Aria Resort & Casino on November 10, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) The Yankees’ biggest needs are at third base and in the bullpen. Arozarena wouldn’t address either of those needs. Still, there could be a fit there if the Yankees believe Bellinger can play a solid center field at this point in his career. With Trent Grisham now a free agent, New York doesn’t really have a primary center fielder. Spencer Jones can also play center field, but he is better in a corner spot. Looking at Randy Arozarena Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – SEPTEMBER 27: Randy Arozarena #56 of the Seattle Mariners lifts his hat as he runs in from the outfield after being pulled from the game during the seventh inning against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 27, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Arozarena is coming off the best season of his career. The outfielder posted 5.7 bWAR and a .281/.381/.484 slash line with 26 home runs and 79 RBI over 154 games with the Seattle Mariners in 2026. While he is a strong hitter, Arozarena struggles defensively. This year, the outfielder posted -2 Defensive Runs Saved and -5 Outs Above Average. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post New York Yankees Interested in 3-Time All-Star Free Agent Outfielder appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Jacoby Brissett throws one of the wackiest INTs for his first pick with Ravens
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Jacoby Brissett throws one of the wackiest INTs for his first pick with Ravens appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jacoby Brissett had a rough opening half as a Baltimore Raven on Monday Night Football. The Ravens QB suffered an awkward fall as one of his linemen was pushed into him as he was throwing. Luckily, he shook that off and avoided any significant injury. Then, he had his first interception as a Raven after quite a wacky play in the second quarter. As Brissett was targeting Ja’Kobi Lane, Chargers cornerback Cam Hart was able to deflect the ball right onto the waiting arms of linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips for the pick . Del'Shawn Phillips COMES UP BIG for the interception 😤 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Chargers take over! pic.twitter.com/yj4ZJjBO0S — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 17, 2026 That interception would prove costly as the Chargers went on to score their second touchdown of the game to bump their lead to 17-7. Omarion Hampton converted a fourth-down on the goal-line for his fourth touchdown of the season. Brissett the Ravens would pull three points back with a field goal right at the end of the first half to cut the lead to 17-10. Aside from his injury scare and wacky pick, Brissett was busy in the first half. He threw the ball 23 times, with 14 completions for 163 yards. Tight ends Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas were his main targets as the two combined for seven catches for 78 yards. The Ravens have been absolutely horrific in the second half during their four-game losing streak . They’ve scored just 10 total points in those four games, seven of which were from a consolation touchdown late against the Jaguars. It remains to be seen if Brissett has what it takes to turn that troubling trend around and win his Ravens debut. item.title: Ravens QB Jacoby Brissett leaves Peyton, Eli Manning stunned with highlight throw
item.description: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Ravens QB Jacoby Brissett leaves Peyton, Eli Manning stunned with highlight throw appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens watched Tre Harris of the Los Angeles Chargers pull off a highlight-reel catch. But quarterback Jacoby Brissett executed a highlight of his own. Which even left Peyton and Eli Manning stunned. Brissett delivered this beautiful lob against LA, amazing the Super Bowl winning quarterbacks during the “Manningcast.” Peyton and Eli are stunned by this great pass from Jacoby Brissett 😤 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “If he floats it with air that corner is going to pick it off.” pic.twitter.com/58fvfO9kRZ — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 17, 2026 Brissett’s throw originally looked like it was going to be intercepted with how it floated. Plus the fact his intended target Rashod Bateman became heavily covered. But Brissett still showed strong trust in Bateman to haul down that pass while down 10-0. Running back Derrick Henry eventually punched in the football past the end zone, cutting the lead to 10-7 during the second quarter. Brissett rose as the fourth different quarterback for rookie head coach Jesse Minter . The former Chargers defensive coordinator has witnessed franchise QB Lamar Jackson endure an injury-ravaged season. Even backup Tyler Huntley has lost the rest of the 2026 season with a severe turf toe injury, arriving in week eight versus the Buffalo Bills. Joe Fagnano briefly took over starting quarterback duties against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 5. But Fagnano settled for just 60 passing yards on 10-of-18 passing with two interceptions. So Brissett earned his Ravens debut against the winless Chargers . He completed 14 passes out of 23 attempts, racking up 163 yards but got picked off once against Del’Shawn Phillips. Baltimore sits in last place in the competitive AFC North standings that now features the Cincinnati Bengals sitting on top with their 7-2 record. The Ravens entered Monday with four straight losses following a strong 4-1 start. item.title: Oregon's Dan Lanning talks Evan Stewart, short week ahead of MSU game
item.description: Oregon football coach Dan Lanning predictably wouldn't go into the specifics of his verbal spat with fifth-year receiver Evan Stewart just before halftime of the Ducks ' win vs. Michigan Nov. 14, but he did offer clarity on the receiver's status vs. Michigan State after Stewart didn't play in the second half. Stewart appeared visibly upset after quarterback Dylan Raiola threw a pass out of bounds on third down with 1:49 left to play in the first half and got into a heated argument with Lanning heading into the locker room. The receiver only played 22 snaps the entire game, compared to 58 for Dakorien Moore and 55 for Jeremiah McClellan, the other starting receivers. "I’ll just say that football in a lot of ways is like a family," Lanning said Nov. 16. "You’ll have disagreements at times. He’s a passionate player, I’m a passionate coach. We’ll keep that within us, but I know how much he wants to do a good job for this team and for himself personally and I have expectations that he can create that moving forward." Stewart missed time earlier this season following his DUII arrest , but has been reliable when he's been on the field, catching 36 passes for 508 yards and four touchdowns in eight games. Lanning said Stewart would be available this week against Michigan State. Lanning also mentioned starting offensive guard Douglas Utu practiced Monday and "is going to be in good shape" following a fourth quarter injury vs. Michigan and running back Jordon Davison, who has missed each of the past two games for Oregon, is out of his boot. Lanning talks short week ahead of travel to Michigan State Though the Spartans have struggled this season, Lanning is expecting a stiff test against former longtime Northwestern coach Pat Fitzgerald's squad, in his first year in East Lansing. He cited toughness and a certain level of physicality that previous Fitzgerald teams have played with that the Ducks will need to match if they want to avoid getting upset Friday night on the road. That, and adapting to a long travel day out to Michigan on a short week. "I think our players understand, like OK, you’re going to get a lot shoved in early in the week and you’ll have to absorb it and be able to play into what do we do well already and how can we build off that?" Lanning said. "What can we carry over that we feel like our players can execute at a high level?" The Ducks and Spartans will meet Nov. 20 in East Lansing at 5 p.m. PT. Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard. You may reach him at adietz@registerguard.com . Want to see more Oregon Ducks coverage? Subscribe to The Register-Guard’s newsletter . This article originally appeared on Register-Guard: Oregon's Dan Lanning talks Evan Stewart, short week ahead of MSU game

item.title: ‘That’s Leadership’ — 3-Time NBA All-Star Rejects Claims Luka Dončić Disrespected Lakers Assistant Coach With Viral Clipboard Grab
item.description: 'That's Leadership' — 3-Time NBA All-Star Rejects Claims Luka Dončić Disrespected Lakers Assistant Coach With Viral Clipboard Grab Former NBA All-Star Gilbert Arenas has come to Luka Dončić’s defense after the Los Angeles Lakers superstar grabbed a clipboard from assistant coach Lindsey Harding during a timeout in Sunday’s 131-123 road win over the Phoenix Suns. The moment went viral as the Lakers nearly blew a 31-point second-half lead, with some interpreting Dončić’s actions as disrespectful toward Harding. Arenas strongly disagreed with that interpretation. LA coach JJ Redick also shed some light on what Dončić was trying to communicate, though the 27-year-old declined to share the specifics. Gilbert Arenas Dissects Luka Dončić’s Viral Clipboard Grab LA led 101-70 late in the third quarter, but Phoenix stormed back and outscored Dončić and Co. 43-27 in the final frame. Along the way, the Lakers entered a timeout up 122-114 with 3:04 remaining. During the stoppage, Dončić took the clipboard from Harding as she and fellow assistant Scott Brooks worked with the coaching staff, then used it to address his teammates directly. Phoenix later pulled within 126-121 with 1:05 left, but Dončić found Quentin Grimes for a 3-pointer to extend LA’s lead back to 8 points. The Slovenian megastar then knocked down a pair of late free throws to help seal the victory. READ MORE: ‘Got Me in Tears,’ ‘Look at JJ Redick’s Face’ — NBA World in Disbelief As Luka Dončić Takes Assistant Coach’s Clipboard As Lakers Nearly Blow 31-Point Lead On Monday’s edition of “Gil’s Arena,” Arenas walked through why he had no issue with the two-time NBA scoring champion taking matters into his own hands. “That’s leadership. The reason it’s leadership is, whatever they’re having a conversation about, he’s trying to show them, right? He’s trying to give them the visual,” Arenas said. “They had the clipboard, so it’s like, ‘Hey, can you give me this [expletive] real quick?’ … So, whatever it is, like, ‘Yo, if I’m driving here, he’s going to slide over; I need you to be here.’ So, he’s showing them there, and that’s what he’s going back to give them and draw the [expletive] y’all going to draw up.” The three-time All-Star also made it clear that the initiative wasn’t meant to undermine the Lakers’ coaching staff: “That’s not like, ‘[Expletive] your play, this is the play we running.’ That’s not that case.” Arenas’ example came from the offensive end, but Redick traced Dončić’s message to a defensive possession. “We had switched [to] zone and Collin Gillespie missed a [3-pointer]; we were soft with our pickup point. He’s a laser; he’s a 4-point line pickup guy. He took a 3 and missed it, but ended up getting an offensive rebound. Luka was just saying just be up versus their lasers,” Redick explained.
