Gillespie came off the bench to lead the Suns with 26 points on 8-for-14 shooting (57.1%), including 5-for-10 from deep (50%). Two of those triples came early in the fourth quarter as Phoenix’s comeback took shape. “That stays in the team, man,” Dončić said of what he told the group. “That will stay in the team. They know what I was communicating.” READ MORE: ‘Totally Disrespectful,’ ‘Undermined the Authority’ — Ex-NFL RB Rips Luka Dončić for ‘Snatching’ Coach’s Clipboard During Lakers-Suns Dončić led the way without his co-star Austin Reaves (heel), posting a game-high 43 points and 9 assists in 36 minutes. He shot 13-for-28 overall (46.4%), 5-for-13 from long range (38.5%) and 12-for-14 from the free-throw line (85.7%). The win completed a perfect four-game road trip and extended the Lakers’ winning streak to eight games. LA (12-2) is now tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the league’s top record. The undermanned Lakers return home against the Charlotte Hornets (4-9) on Tuesday, looking to extend their victory run to nine outings. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Broncos’ Bo Nix hilariously reacts to Peyton Manning’s record without too much effort
item.description: Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Broncos’ Bo Nix hilariously reacts to Peyton Manning’s record without too much effort appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Broncos are 7-2, tied with the Kansas City Chiefs for first place in the AFC West, with several problems to fix during the bye week, especially on Bo Nix ’s offense. Nix and company have been solid, but have lacked the explosive plays previously seen heading into Week 11’s home matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders, which comes on the heels of a failed NFL Trade Deadline deal . Nix took some time out of his bye week schedule to join brothers Peyton and Eli Manning during the Monday Night Football game between the Ravens and Chargers. Eli Manning pointed out a hilarious stat that Nix surpassed his brother in without even trying. “Peyton in his four years in Denver rushed for -55 yards, so how much did it mean to you to pass Peyton on the all-time list in your very first game? Was that special?” Eli Manning asked Nix, which caused Peyton Manning to start cracking up with laughter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “My first run, being able to get a couple yards on the first run and pass that mark was pretty special,” Nix said. “It was a great accomplishment at the time, and hopefully there are a couple more rushing records to break of his,” the Broncos’ current QB said. Nix has 902 rushing yards with the Broncos in 2 1/2 seasons, second all-time in franchise history behind John Elway, who finished his Denver career with 3,402 yards rushing. Nix has gained a reputation as a clutch player for his early career exploits with the Broncos, soon he will have a chance to show them off again with a Week 11 tilt scheduled on November 22 against the Raiders in Denver. item.title: Darius Garland Believes Clippers Are Moving in Right Direction After Win vs Hornets
item.description: Following a woeful start to the season, the Los Angeles Clippers look like they are figuring some things out. The Clippers (4-8) lost seven straight games after beating the Sacramento Kings in their season opener. However, they have since steadied the ship and won three of their last four — including two in a row. Los Angeles backed up its huge home win against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Friday with another against the Charlotte Hornets at Intuit Dome on Sunday. The Clippers triumphed 113-105 behind 27 points, six rebounds, and seven assists from star point guard Darius Garland. Momentum Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images It doesn't take a lot for elite athletes to find some confidence and start building momentum. The Clippers are proving that right now. Garland acknowledged that the OKC win was massive for the team, whether the former champions are shorthanded or not. "Coming into [the Hornets] game, finishing it pretty well, that was another step [towards] some good success," he said . "We're starting to figure out what we want to do on the offensive and defensive end. We're [getting] comfortable with that." Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Although Garland is still being pestered by turnover issues (4.9 per game), he did enough all over the floor to set the tone for the Clippers against Charlotte. Garland, who leads L.A. in scoring with 21.3 points, shot 10-for-18 from the field (3-for-7 3PT) and was a team high +12 despite committing six giveaways. The Clippers were extremely efficient as a collective, shooting 55 percent from the field and 52 percent from beyond the arc. They nailed 16 triples while holding the Hornets to just 38 percent shooting (33% 3PT). Charlotte made one more three-pointer than the Clippers on 21 more attempts. Better In The Clutch Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The biggest sign of the Clippers' improvement was their execution down the stretch. The hosts locked up the win behind a 29-22 fourth-quarter run, finally pulling away after a back-and-forth contest. The Clippers racked up 32 assists on 41 made field goals. They played team basketball , with everybody chipping in. Four bench players scored in double figures en route to 55 second unit points. Derrick Jones Jr. was the only other starter with 10+ points. He dropped 13 on 5-for-5 shooting (3-for-3 3PT). Off the pine, Max Strus led the way with 14 points on 5-for-8 shooting (4-for-5 3PT). Isaiah Jackson added 13 points (4-for-5 FG), three blocks, and one steal. Gradey Dick (12) and Keaton Wagler (12) combined for 24 points. Dick went 2-for-2 from deep while Wagler notched four rebounds and five assists. The Clippers led by as much as 17 points. They will look to continue their ascent against the Utah Jazz (1-13) on Tuesday.

item.title: New Zealand squad for India Test series 2026: Full updates and team lists for NZ vs IND Tests
item.description: New Zealand squad for India Test series 2026: Full updates and team lists for NZ vs IND Tests originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: New Zealand have announced their Test squad, but fitness doubts linger around a few names. Coach Rob Walter has spoken about the summer ahead and the crowds he expects. Crucial World Test Championship points are in play, and India cannot afford to fall short to stay in the race. Mitchell Santner ruled out of Test series with an injury. New Zealand Test squad for India Test series 2026 New Zealand named a 14-man squad for the two-Test series against India, and three of the players on the list are still working their way back from injuries. Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell have all been picked even though none of them had fully recovered. The selectors appear to have decided that these three are too important to leave out, and they will be hoping each player is match-ready by the time the first Test arrives. Conway picked up a concussion during a training session just before the ongoing ODI series began. Ravindra has been dealing with a shoulder problem since September, when he was hurt during a commercial photoshoot. Blundell, for his part, is recovering from a quadriceps issue. Head coach Rob Walter has already turned his attention to a busy home season, and he is pleased that a big-name side like India will be the visitors. MORE: 'I'm just sick of it': Kane Williamson admits frustration with 'good guy' label attached to him and NZ cricketers “This series marks the start of an exciting summer of Test cricket for the Blackcaps. The squad is largely consistent with the team that competed in England earlier this year, so it’ll be great to be back together to try and recreate some of that success on home soil,” he said. The coach was equally happy with the turnout at the white-ball games so far, and he hopes the same energy will be there when the longer format begins. Fans have shown up in good numbers during the limited-overs matches, which has lifted the mood in the dressing room. “We’ve experienced great crowds so far during the white-ball series, and we’re really looking forward to having that support during the Tests,” Walter added. New Zealand currently sit on top of the World Test Championship standings, and a few more wins against India would only make their position stronger. Shubman Gill’s side are a fair way behind in fourth place, and they cannot afford to slip to stay in the race for a berth in the top-two spots. After the conclusion of the ODI series, New Zealand confirmed Mitchell Santner has been ruled out of the Test series after picking up a hand injury during the fifth ODI. Spin-bowling all-rounder Dean Foxcroft has been called up as Santner's replacement. The selectors appear to have decided that these three are too important to leave out, and they will be hoping each player is match-ready by the time the first Test arrives. Conway picked up a concussion during a training session just before the ongoing ODI series began. Ravindra has been dealing with a shoulder problem since September, when he was hurt during a commercial photoshoot. Blundell, for his part, is recovering from a quadriceps issue. Head coach Rob Walter has already turned his attention to a busy home season, and he is pleased that a big-name side like India will be the visitors. MORE: 'I'm just sick of it': Kane Williamson admits frustration with 'good guy' label attached to him and NZ cricketers “This series marks the start of an exciting summer of Test cricket for the Blackcaps. The squad is largely consistent with the team that competed in England earlier this year, so it’ll be great to be back together to try and recreate some of that success on home soil,” he said. The coach was equally happy with the turnout at the white-ball games so far, and he hopes the same energy will be there when the longer format begins. Fans have shown up in good numbers during the limited-overs matches, which has lifted the mood in the dressing room. “We’ve experienced great crowds so far during the white-ball series, and we’re really looking forward to having that support during the Tests,” Walter added. New Zealand currently sit on top of the World Test Championship standings, and a few more wins against India would only make their position stronger. Shubman Gill’s side are a fair way behind in fourth place, and they cannot afford to slip to stay in the race for a berth in the top-two spots. After the conclusion of the ODI series, New Zealand confirmed Mitchell Santner has been ruled out of the Test series after picking up a hand injury during the fifth ODI. Spin-bowling all-rounder Dean Foxcroft has been called up as Santner's replacement. MORE: India squad for New Zealand Test series 2026: Full updates and team lists for NZ vs IND Tests Full New Zealand squad for the two-Test series against India Tom Latham (captain) Tom Blundell (recovering from quadriceps problem) Devon Conway (recovering from concussion) Jacob Duffy Matt Henry Kyle Jamieson Daryl Mitchell Henry Nicholls Glenn Phillips Rachin Ravindra (recovering from shoulder injury) 𝙼̶𝚒̶𝚝̶𝚌̶𝚑̶𝚎̶𝚕̶𝚕̶ ̶𝚂̶𝚊̶𝚗̶𝚝̶𝚗̶𝚎̶𝚛̶ (Hand injury) Nathan Smith Blair Tickner Will Young Dean Foxcroft Why New Zealand’s injury gamble on Conway, Ravindra and Blundell makes sense New Zealand’s decision to include three players who are still recovering is a calculated risk, and on balance it looks like a sensible one. Conway, Ravindra and Blundell are all established names who have done well for the side, and leaving them out too early could have cost the team experience at a time when the schedule is packed. With ten Tests lined up before March, depth will matter just as much as quality. The bigger point is continuity. Walter has said the group is close to the one that did well in England, and that kind of stability is rare in modern Test cricket. Sides that keep their core together tend to build trust in the dressing room, and that trust often shows up in tight sessions when the pressure is on. Still, the medical staff will need to be careful. A concussion is not something any team should rush, whereas shoulder and quadriceps problems can easily flare up if a player returns too soon. The squad has only 14 names, which means there is little room to carry anyone who is not fully fit, and the management should be ready with a firm plan if one of the three misses out. There is also the matter of expectations. Playing at home, leading the Championship table and backed by big crowds, New Zealand will be seen as favourites by many. That brings its own pressure, but Walter’s talk about focusing on good cricket rather than points is the right message to send. If the three injured players come through their recovery on time, this squad has every chance of making the summer a memorable one. item.title: Steelers Legend Mike Tomlin Reveals Why He Would Never Check on NFL HCs Going Through Tough Times
item.description: ATLANTA, GA – OCTOBER 11: Mike Tomlin before the Sunday evening NFL, American Football Herren, USA game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Baltimore Ravens on October 11, 2026 at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire NFL: OCT 11 Ravens at Falcons EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon9532610119 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin pulled himself away from the coaching job in the NFL after being in the business for over two decades. That’s a long time to know the league to the core. Given his experience, Tomlin opened up about the unusual approach to friendship within the coaching fraternity. “In our business, man, if you’re real friends, you don’t check on them, because checking on them is like you don’t believe they can hack it,” shared Tomlin on the Not Just Football with Cam Heyward podcast. “Like me and Raheem Morris specifically, I would never call him when he’s going through a tough time. He would never, ever, ever call me if I’m going through a tough time, because like, ‘No, man, don’t check on me. Check on the bear.’ “It’s just the mentality that I have in my coaching friend group. The relationships are what they are, man, they’re deep and they’re real, but no, we don’t check on each other. That’s a display of weakness.” Tomlin’s first exposure to coaching in the NFL came with the University of Cincinnati when he served as the defensive backs coach for one season in 1999. After that came the Tampa Bay Buccaneers stint, where he worked from 2001 to 2005. That’s when he crossed paths with Raheem Morris. Tomlin's philosophy on coaching camaraderie just revealed a surprising truth about NFL leadership. Subscribe to stay updated on the mindsets shaping the league's most respected voices. Talking about their bond? They shared a strong friendship that stayed even though their roads led in different directions. Morris became the Tampa Bay head coach in 2009 while Tomlin was in charge of the Steelers from 2007. Back in 2010, their teams were winning, but Tomlin and Morris still found a reason to challenge each other. Shortly after Pittsburgh and Tampa Bay claimed road victories to stay unbeaten, the two coaches exchanged some pointed text messages. The conversation captured the competitive edge in their friendship as the Steelers and Buccaneers prepared to meet in Tampa. “We’re coming,” messaged Tomlin “Good,” responded Morris. In another interview, Morris opened up about what Tomlin meant to him. “Man, I can’t stand this man. He’s an archenemy of mine”, he said in a clearly unserious manner, via the team’s YouTube channel. “We got the chance to work with each other for a couple of years, and we remained really good friends off the field-and on the field, I can’t stand him.” But when Morris hit a rough patch in Tampa Bay, Tomlin left his former colleague alone to face his challenges and fight his own battles rather than give his peer sympathy or reassurance. Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire NFL: OCT 11 Ravens at Falcons EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon9532610119 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin pulled himself away from the coaching job in the NFL after being in the business for over two decades. That’s a long time to know the league to the core. Given his experience, Tomlin opened up about the unusual approach to friendship within the coaching fraternity. “In our business, man, if you’re real friends, you don’t check on them, because checking on them is like you don’t believe they can hack it,” shared Tomlin on the Not Just Football with Cam Heyward podcast. “Like me and Raheem Morris specifically, I would never call him when he’s going through a tough time. He would never, ever, ever call me if I’m going through a tough time, because like, ‘No, man, don’t check on me. Check on the bear.’ “It’s just the mentality that I have in my coaching friend group. The relationships are what they are, man, they’re deep and they’re real, but no, we don’t check on each other. That’s a display of weakness.” Tomlin’s first exposure to coaching in the NFL came with the University of Cincinnati when he served as the defensive backs coach for one season in 1999. After that came the Tampa Bay Buccaneers stint, where he worked from 2001 to 2005. That’s when he crossed paths with Raheem Morris. Tomlin's philosophy on coaching camaraderie just revealed a surprising truth about NFL leadership. Subscribe to stay updated on the mindsets shaping the league's most respected voices. Talking about their bond? They shared a strong friendship that stayed even though their roads led in different directions. Morris became the Tampa Bay head coach in 2009 while Tomlin was in charge of the Steelers from 2007. Back in 2010, their teams were winning, but Tomlin and Morris still found a reason to challenge each other. Shortly after Pittsburgh and Tampa Bay claimed road victories to stay unbeaten, the two coaches exchanged some pointed text messages. The conversation captured the competitive edge in their friendship as the Steelers and Buccaneers prepared to meet in Tampa. “We’re coming,” messaged Tomlin “Good,” responded Morris. In another interview, Morris opened up about what Tomlin meant to him. “Man, I can’t stand this man. He’s an archenemy of mine”, he said in a clearly unserious manner, via the team’s YouTube channel. “We got the chance to work with each other for a couple of years, and we remained really good friends off the field-and on the field, I can’t stand him.” But when Morris hit a rough patch in Tampa Bay, Tomlin left his former colleague alone to face his challenges and fight his own battles rather than give his peer sympathy or reassurance. In January 2012, Morris was fired as a head coach from the Buccaneers. Under him, the team failed to recover from its midseason struggles, losing 10 straight games before closing the campaign with a 45-24 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons. It marked the franchise’s longest losing streak in one season since 1977. But as Tomlin shared, he did not check on Morris even once. That doesn’t mean Tomlin did not have any role to play in his life. Morris picked up an important coaching habit from Tomlin: never limit your understanding of football to one side of the ball. Tomlin, a former college wide receiver at William & Mary, frequently attended offensive meetings, prompting Morris to do the same. The initiative became a defining part of Morris’ coaching philosophy, allowing him to move between offensive and defensive responsibilities. So, when Atlanta assigned him to its wide receivers room in 2016, the decision may have surprised some, but Morris was well prepared for the challenge. “The first opportunity I got to coach (offense) was here with Dan Quinn, and really that was full force,” Morris said. “No hesitation going into it because of those moments with Mike Tomlin and thinking about the background knowledge that you want to have being a coach on defense, having knowledge to coach on offense, and it certainly serves me well right now in the position I’m in now.” So the relationship among the coaches, as Tomlin stressed, is strong and deep. However, at the same time, they show respect by trusting each other to overcome difficult situations without needing emotional check-ins. Speaking to reporters before Monday’s game against the Houston Rockets, Larsson said he expects to play Wednesday when Miami hosts the Milwaukee Bucks. The update came after Larsson completed a pregame workout designed to test his recovery. “I just caught a cold in Utah,” Larsson said, according to The Athletic. “Just bad luck.” Larsson has been sidelined since becoming ill during Miami’s road trip. However, the 25-year-old believes he has avoided the complications that prolonged a similar illness during the preseason. Larsson missed several preseason games because of an illness but recovered in time for Miami’s regular-season opener against Minnesota on Oct. 21. He told reporters Monday that his current illness has been less severe. “The other one was worse because I tried to come back too early,” Larsson said. “This one, I just had a cold and a sore throat, so just trying to wait for that to go away and now I’m back, up and running.” Larsson’s expected return would give Miami back one of its most versatile perimeter players. Through 11 games this season, the Swedish guard is averaging 11.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.3 steals in 29.5 minutes per game. He’s shooting 46.8% from the field and a career-best 46.9% from 3-point range. His outside shooting has improved considerably from last season, when he connected on 32.3% of his 3-point attempts. However, the 25-year-old believes he has avoided the complications that prolonged a similar illness during the preseason. Pelle Larsson Reveals Expected Heat Return Date Getty Pelle Larsson of the Miami Heat holds off Josh Okogie of the Utah Jazz as he brings the ball up the court during the first half at the Delta Center on November 10, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. Larsson missed several preseason games because of an illness but recovered in time for Miami’s regular-season opener against Minnesota on Oct. 21. He told reporters Monday that his current illness has been less severe. “The other one was worse because I tried to come back too early,” Larsson said. “This one, I just had a cold and a sore throat, so just trying to wait for that to go away and now I’m back, up and running.” Larsson’s expected return would give Miami back one of its most versatile perimeter players. Larsson has also provided dependable ballhandling and defensive activity within Erik Spoelstra’s rotation. Still, Miami has not officially cleared him for Wednesday’s matchup. Before Monday’s game, Spoelstra said Larsson needed another workout before the team could determine his readiness. “Making progress,” Spoelstra told reporters . “He’s going to get a real good workout today, and we’ll see how he responds tomorrow.” Erik Spoelstra Praises Myron Gardner During Larsson’s Absence With Larsson unavailable, Myron Gardner has stepped into Miami’s starting lineup. The opportunity has allowed Gardner to showcase the relentless defensive effort that earned Spoelstra’s trust. Asked about Gardner’s contributions, the Heat coach praised his energy and preparation. “He’s constant energy,” Spoelstra said. “It’s not something that he has to summon up. I mean, that’s who he is to his core.” Spoelstra added that Gardner brings the same intensity to practices and other team activities. “And this group needs that,” he said. item.title: Bob Baffert Prepares Kentucky Derby Hopeful Kivo At Del Mar
item.description: Mike Pegram, Karl Watson and Paul Weitman’s Kivo and jockey Emisael Jaramillo win the $100,000 Bob Hope Stakes Sunday, November 15, 2026 at Del Mar Thoroughbred Club, Del Mar, CA. The two-year-old son of Omaha Beach is trained by Hall of Famer Bob Baffert. Benoit Photo BENOIT PHOTO Nobody has been better at developing young horses than Bob Baffert. With a record six wins in the Kentucky Derby, the most trips to the winner’s circle in the Preakness (8), two Triple Crown champions (American Pharoah 2015, Justify 2018), and the largest number of winners in the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile (7), the numbers tell the story for this Hall of Fame conditioner. Now, Big Race Bob appears to be at it again as he is cultivating another talented two-year-old named Kivo at his familiar launching pad, Del Mar. Powerful Score in Bob Hope Stakes At Del Mar Puts Kivo In The Spotlight The 2027 Kentucky Derby may seem a long way off because in reality it is. As has been long established however, it is never too soon to start dreaming of the first Saturday in May. A big run by the Bob Baffert trained Kivo in the Bob Hope Stakes at Del Mar has added this son of Omaha Beach to the list of Derby hopefuls. Breaking alertly from the gates in this seven-furlong affair, Kivo settled just off a solid early pace (22.9 opening quarter, 45.94 half mile). Keeping his mount in the clear, jockey Emisael Jaramillo stayed outside the frontrunners and at the top of the stretch he moved to the lead. Rolling past the pacesetters, Kivo answered the call and strolled past the wire a widening 3 ¼ lengths ahead of six others. This marked his second win in a row on dirt from three career starts. “Kivo is improving in every start he makes”, says Bob Baffert, who has won the Bob Hope Stakes a record eight times. “Distance should not be a problem and we look forward to stretching him out. He is a beautiful mover and his only loss was a race on turf where we felt like he really needed to give him a start.” Trainer Bob Baffert, left, has used Del Mar as a training ground for many of his fantastic young horses over the years. BENOIT PHOTO Del Mar Has Been A Place Of Good Beginnings For Baffert The Bob Hope Stakes is a race of note because Baffert has used the Seaside Oval as a place to cultivate young colts. Four of Baffert’s six Kentucky Derby winners made starts where the turf meets the surf before galloping to glory as a three-year-old. Many other notables from the Baffert barn, like former Bob Hope winners Nysos and Mucho Gusto, used Del Mar as their launching pad to graded stakes stardom. Now joining stablemate Hughes, who won both the Best Pal Stakes and Del Mar Futurity this summer, Kivo has made the list of Kentucky Derby hopefuls conditioned by Bob Baffert. “Del Mar is the best place to grow two-year-olds”, says Baffert. The track conditions are always great and you seldom miss any training because of weather.” Kivo is owned by Karl Watson. Mike Peagram, and Paul Weitman. He was purchased as a

Now joining stablemate Hughes, who won both the Best Pal Stakes and Del Mar Futurity this summer, Kivo has made the list of Kentucky Derby hopefuls conditioned by Bob Baffert. “Del Mar is the best place to grow two-year-olds”, says Baffert. The track conditions are always great and you seldom miss any training because of weather.” Kivo is owned by Karl Watson. Mike Peagram, and Paul Weitman. He was purchased as a yearling for $350,000 at the Keeneland sale and has now earned $100,600 on the track. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Illinois coach hints at dirty play by UCLA after quarterback suffers broken nose
item.description: Illinois head coach, Bret Bielema broke his silence on Monday night, after UCLA’s 22-14 victory on Friday night. During the Fighting Illini’s final possession of the game, quarterback Katin Houser was sacked for a seven-yard loss and was removed from the game with a bloody and broken nose. Bielema alluded that when a pile of Bruins defenders got on top of him, UCLA defenders took a dirty shot. “I was a little hot. I saw something. Turned it into the league, and the league’s got it,” Bielema said to reporters. “I know before that play, he was good-looking, unbroken-nose, and an unconcussed player, and came out of it on a different side.” #illini HC Bret Bielema turned in Katin Houser's final UCLA play to the conference. "I was a little hot. I saw something. Turn it into the league, and the league's got it. I know before that play, he was a good-looking, unbroken nose and unconcussed player, and came out of it on… pic.twitter.com/8WYxHpqvNn — Carson Gourdie (@GourdieReport) November 16, 2026 Illinois quarterback Katin Houser being sacked by a group of UCLA defenders. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong “Nothing happened during the tackle, during the pile. So everything else will sort itself out,” Bielema said. Backup quarterback Carson Boyd finished the game in place of Houser and threw two straight incompletions to end the game. Houser had the Bruins on the edge of their seats, as he was on the verge of snapping UCLA’s perfect record. In the second half, the Illinois quarterback provided heroics that included two touchdown passes to keep them in the game. Houser completed 16 of 34 passes for 176 yards and threw three interceptions, two of which were to Bruins cornerback Scooter Jackson, who was crowned the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week. Illinois quarterback Katin Houser during Friday’s game against UCLA. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong Scooter Jackson reacts to his second interception of the game against Illinois on Friday. Getty Images Having an opportunity to take a late lead, Jackson’s most important interception of the game happened during the final three minutes, when he picked off Houser on the UCLA 40-yard line and returned the ball down to the Illinois 19-yard line. The Illinois defense held the Bruins from converting a first down and forced them to settle for a 37-yard field goal off the leg of Matheen Bhaghani. Illinois received the ball one more time during the final two minutes of the game but couldn’t capitalize on it after Houser’s exit.

item.title: 4 Reasons Why The Rockets Fell Short Against The Heat In Lopsided Loss
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Houston Rockets suffered a disappointing 128-110 loss to the Miami Heat , struggling to match Miami’s heart on both ends. Despite a strong rebounding performance and strong nights from Alperen Sengun and Kevin Durant , Houston never found a consistent answer for the Heat’s balanced attack behind Giannis Antetokounmpo . Sengun finished with 23 points on an efficient 8-11 shooting, while Durant added 22 points. However, the Rockets struggled from beyond the arc, committed too many turnovers, and allowed Miami to generate easy opportunities in transition. The Heat, meanwhile, received contributions across the roster. Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 20 points and 13 rebounds, Davion Mitchell delivered 16 points and 10 assists, and Klay Thompson knocked down five three-pointers. Here are four reasons why Houston fell short against Miami. 1. The Rockets Couldn’t Keep Up With Miami’s Three-Point Shooting The biggest difference between these teams was their shooting from beyond the arc. Miami connected on 18 of its 50 three-point attempts, good for 36.0%, while Houston made just 10 of 36 attempts at 27.8%. That eight-three-pointer difference was enormous in a game decided by 18 points. The Heat consistently generated perimeter opportunities and had multiple players capable of converting them. Klay Thompson led the way with 17 points, shooting 5-8 from three-point range. Andrew Wiggins added three triples, while Bobby Portis and Simone Fontecchio each contributed two. Houston, by comparison, struggled to establish any consistent perimeter rhythm. Durant made two three-pointers, VanVleet added two, and Jabari Smith Jr. connected on just one of his four attempts. The Rockets’ inability to match Miami’s outside shooting ultimately made it difficult to stay competitive. 2. Miami’s Defensive Pressure Disrupted Houston’s Offense Houston’s 52 rebounds might suggest the Rockets controlled the game physically, but Miami was far more effective at turning defensive possessions into advantages. The Heat recorded 11 steals and eight blocks, compared to just four steals and two blocks for Houston. Miami also forced 14 Rockets turnovers while committing only nine itself. That difference created additional scoring opportunities for the Heat and prevented Houston from establishing a comfortable offensive rhythm. Davion Mitchell was particularly effective, recording 16 points, 10 assists, and four steals without committing a turnover. Wiggins also contributed three steals and three blocks, showcasing Miami’s defensive versatility. The Heat’s pressure extended beyond individual performances. item.content:encoded: Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Houston Rockets suffered a disappointing 128-110 loss to the Miami Heat , struggling to match Miami’s heart on both ends. Despite a strong rebounding performance and strong nights from Alperen Sengun and Kevin Durant , Houston never found a consistent answer for the Heat’s balanced attack behind Giannis Antetokounmpo . Sengun finished with 23 points on an efficient 8-11 shooting, while Durant added 22 points. However, the Rockets struggled from beyond the arc, committed too many turnovers, and allowed Miami to generate easy opportunities in transition. The Heat, meanwhile, received contributions across the roster. Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 20 points and 13 rebounds, Davion Mitchell delivered 16 points and 10 assists, and Klay Thompson knocked down five three-pointers. Here are four reasons why Houston fell short against Miami. 1. The Rockets Couldn’t Keep Up With Miami’s Three-Point Shooting The biggest difference between these teams was their shooting from beyond the arc. Miami connected on 18 of its 50 three-point attempts, good for 36.0%, while Houston made just 10 of 36 attempts at 27.8%. That eight-three-pointer difference was enormous in a game decided by 18 points. The Heat consistently generated perimeter opportunities and had multiple players capable of converting them. Klay Thompson led the way with 17 points, shooting 5-8 from three-point range. Andrew Wiggins added three triples, while Bobby Portis and Simone Fontecchio each contributed two. Houston, by comparison, struggled to establish any consistent perimeter rhythm. Durant made two three-pointers, VanVleet added two, and Jabari Smith Jr. connected on just one of his four attempts. The Rockets’ inability to match Miami’s outside shooting ultimately made it difficult to stay competitive. 2. Miami’s Defensive Pressure Disrupted Houston’s Offense Houston’s 52 rebounds might suggest the Rockets controlled the game physically, but Miami was far more effective at turning defensive possessions into advantages. The Heat recorded 11 steals and eight blocks, compared to just four steals and two blocks for Houston. Miami also forced 14 Rockets turnovers while committing only nine itself. That difference created additional scoring opportunities for the Heat and prevented Houston from establishing a comfortable offensive rhythm. Davion Mitchell was particularly effective, recording 16 points, 10 assists, and four steals without committing a turnover. Wiggins also contributed three steals and three blocks, showcasing Miami’s defensive versatility. The Heat’s pressure extended beyond individual performances. Miami scored 24 fast-break points compared to Houston’s eight, turning defensive stops into easy offense. 3. Houston Didn’t Get Enough Consistent Production Beyond Sengun and Durant Sengun and Durant did their part, but Houston needed more from the rest of its rotation. Sengun finished with 23 points and seven rebounds on 8-11 shooting, while Durant contributed 22 points on 8-19 shooting. However, the supporting cast struggled. Jabari Smith Jr. finished with 12 points and 10 rebounds but shot just 4-12 from the field. Tari Eason added seven points on 2-8 shooting, while VanVleet managed eight points despite distributing six assists. The Rockets also received limited offensive production from their bench. Isaiah Crawford scored 11 points and grabbed 10 rebounds, but no Houston reserve reached double figures beyond him. Miami, on the other hand, received 17 points from Wiggins, 16 from Portis, 14 from Myron Gardner, and 14 from Tim Hardaway Jr. That depth made a significant difference. Houston had two productive offensive options, but Miami consistently found contributions from different players. 4. Miami’s Ball Movement and Interior Offense Were Too Much to Handle The Heat were more efficient offensively and consistently found ways to attack Houston’s defense. Miami shot 50.0% from the field, compared to Houston’s 41.3%, while recording 29 assists against the Rockets’ 23. Giannis was particularly effective, finishing with 20 points, 13 rebounds, and six assists on 8-11 shooting. His ability to attack the basket and create opportunities for teammates helped Miami maintain offensive balance. The Heat also dominated the paint, scoring 54 points compared to Houston’s 44. They complemented that interior production with their perimeter shooting, making it difficult for the Rockets to prioritize one area defensively. Houston actually won the rebounding battle 52-40, including a commanding 21-13 advantage in offensive rebounds. However, those extra possessions weren’t enough to overcome Miami’s superior shooting and offensive execution.

item.title: ‘Teachers, doctors won’t pay tax when I become gov’
item.description: By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo LAGOS—Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr. Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes, if elected governor, saying his administration will use increased Federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and welfare of residents. Doherty, who made the promise during an interview on a Channels Television programme, said he would also introduce a tax card that would enable residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation. He said: “When I am governor, I will transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two groups will not pay tax. “Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation. This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you.” The PDP candidate also promised free education, saying the funds available to the state would enable him to implement the policy. Justifying the proposed tax exemption for doctors, he said: “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break.” He described teachers as critical to the state’s future, arguing that they must receive proper training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities. Doherty further condemned attacks on political activities and disclosed that some people he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge. He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he would visit the Department of State Services, DSS. The post ‘Teachers, doctors won’t pay tax when I become gov’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Abia approves ₦1.04bn for SMEs, reviews ASEPA workers’ pay
item.description: …₦382.9m disbursed to 31 businesses By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has secured approval for ₦1.041 billion in intervention funding for small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs), in a move aimed at expanding businesses, stimulating job creation and improving access to affordable credit. Of the amount, ₦382.9 million has already been disbursed to 29 micro-enterprises and two small and medium-scale businesses, while another ₦206.7 million in approved applications is undergoing documentation ahead of disbursement. The state government also announced a review of the remuneration of ad-hoc workers engaged by the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA), with the new payment structure taking effect from November 2026. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, who disclosed the developments during the weekly briefing on the State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia, said the SME intervention was being implemented through the Bank of Industry (BOI). Kanu, represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Fredinald Ekeoma, said the initiative was part of Governor Alex Otti’s administration’s efforts to strengthen the state’s productive sector and create sustainable employment opportunities. Providing further details, Commissioner for Industries and SMEs, Mazi Mike Akpara, said the outstanding approved facilities would be released once beneficiaries fulfilled the necessary conditions, including documentation and provision of guarantors and collateral, where applicable. He stressed that access to the intervention was not restricted by political affiliation, insisting that any genuine business operating in Abia was eligible. “Whether you belong to the Labour Party, PDP or APC, we are not concerned about that. Once you are doing business in Abia and can provide evidence of your business operations, you are eligible to benefit. “SMEs are the engine of the economy, and this initiative is intended to encourage and strengthen them,” Akpara said. He said interested businesses could access the programme through the Ministry of Industries and SMEs at the Nnamdi Azikiwe Secretariat, Umuahia, or the BOI office in Aba. Akpara described the facility as a major relief for local entrepreneurs, given its relatively low interest rates of 8.5 per cent for overdrafts and 7.5 per cent for other facilities, with a three-year repayment period. He contrasted the rates with commercial bank lending rates, which he said could rise to between 28 and 30 per cent, arguing that the intervention would ease the financing burden on businesses and improve their capacity to expand. In another development, Kanu said the Ministry of Industries and SMEs had verified and documented more than 110 workshops and 120 shops at the Ohiya-Umuogo-Nsukwe Industrial Cluster. In another development, Kanu said the Ministry of Industries and SMEs had verified and documented more than 110 workshops and 120 shops at the Ohiya-Umuogo-Nsukwe Industrial Cluster. He said the exercise aligned with Goal Eight of the Sustainable Development Goals, which focuses on inclusive economic growth, productive employment and decent work. On the forthcoming AfrICANDO 2026 conference, the Information Commissioner announced that Governor Otti would formally declare the global event open on Tuesday, November 17, at the International Conference Centre, Umuahia. He said the conference would attract local and international participants, offering opportunities for investment partnerships, trade expansion and business development across different sectors. Kanu urged the media to give the event adequate coverage, noting that Abia was open to investors seeking viable business opportunities. The Commissioner also dismissed any suggestion that ongoing political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections had slowed down governance in the state. He said the machinery of government remained fully operational despite the distractions associated with electioneering, adding that preparations for the 2027 fiscal year were nearing completion. “In this connection, we affirm that the Abia State 2027 Budget is almost ready for presentation to the Abia State House of Assembly,” he said. item.title: Dry season farming: Shettima directs swift release of 3m fertiliser bags nationwide
item.description: ‎—Orders ONSA to monitor declared stocks ahead of distribution ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Vice President Senator Kashim Shettima has directed relevant government agencies and stakeholders in the fertiliser industry to expedite arrangements for the production and release of over three million bags of fertiliser to farmers across the country ahead of the forthcoming dry-season farming. ‎ ‎The directive followed President Bola Tinubu’s approval of funding under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative, aimed at making fertiliser more affordable, boosting food production and reviving Nigeria’s fertiliser blending industry. ‎ ‎The Vice President gave the directive on Monday at the Presidential Villa during a meeting with stakeholders in the fertiliser sector in Abuja, where the Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) disclosed that available raw materials could support the production of approximately three million bags of NPK fertiliser within the next few weeks. ‎ ‎He also directed the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) to verify and track fertiliser stocks declared by stakeholders to ensure transparency, accountability and a hitch-free distribution exercise. ‎ ‎He further urged the NSA’s office to ensure that farming communities in states facing security challenges are not neglected in the distribution programme, stressing the need for the intervention to reach farmers in vulnerable and hard-to-access areas. ‎ ‎Speaking on the broader economic importance of the presidential intervention, the Vice President said revitalising Nigeria’s fertiliser industry would strengthen agricultural productivity while creating jobs and supporting rural livelihoods. ‎ ‎”A strong fertilizer value chain supports hundreds of thousands of direct and indirect jobs. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: ‎—Orders ONSA to monitor declared stocks ahead of distribution ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Vice President Senator Kashim Shettima has directed relevant government agencies and stakeholders in the fertiliser industry to expedite arrangements for the production and release of over three million bags of fertiliser to farmers across the country ahead of the forthcoming dry-season farming. ‎ ‎The directive followed President Bola Tinubu’s approval of funding under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative, aimed at making fertiliser more affordable, boosting food production and reviving Nigeria’s fertiliser blending industry. ‎ ‎The Vice President gave the directive on Monday at the Presidential Villa during a meeting with stakeholders in the fertiliser sector in Abuja, where the Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) disclosed that available raw materials could support the production of approximately three million bags of NPK fertiliser within the next few weeks. ‎ ‎He also directed the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) to verify and track fertiliser stocks declared by stakeholders to ensure transparency, accountability and a hitch-free distribution exercise. ‎ ‎He further urged the NSA’s office to ensure that farming communities in states facing security challenges are not neglected in the distribution programme, stressing the need for the intervention to reach farmers in vulnerable and hard-to-access areas. ‎ ‎Speaking on the broader economic importance of the presidential intervention, the Vice President said revitalising Nigeria’s fertiliser industry would strengthen agricultural productivity while creating jobs and supporting rural livelihoods. ‎ ‎”A strong fertilizer value chain supports hundreds of thousands of direct and indirect jobs. Revitalizing this sector is therefore important not only for agriculture but also for employment, rural livelihoods and economic activities across the country,” he stated. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima expressed concern that many of the country’s fertiliser blending plants were operating below capacity despite the growing demand for affordable agricultural inputs. ‎ ‎”Today, many of our fertilizer blending plants are operating below capacity at the same time the high cost of fertilizer continues to increase the cost of production for our farmers,” he observed. ‎ ‎According to him, President Tinubu’s intervention is designed to address these challenges by stimulating domestic production, restoring jobs and making fertiliser available to farmers at affordable prices. ‎ ‎”The government wants to support the rehabilitation and full utilization of our fertilizer blending capacity. We want the factories producing, we want workers back to work. We want transporters, warehouse, and agro-dealers to be engaged again,” he said. ‎ ‎The Vice President emphasised that farmers remained the principal beneficiaries of the initiative, noting that the Federal Government would purchase fertiliser produced by Nigerian blending companies and make it available at affordable prices. ‎ ‎”But ultimately the Nigerian farmer is at the centre of this initiative. Under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative, government intends to purchase fertilizers produced by Nigerian blenders and make it available to our farmers at affordable prices,” he added. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima thanked industry operators and other stakeholders for their willingness to partner with the government, stressing that the success of the intervention would depend on timely production, effective coordination and efficient distribution. ‎ ‎”Every stakeholder is expected to prepare accordingly in ensuring the success of the Presidential mandate to deliver fertilizer to farmers for the fast approaching dry-season farming,” he charged. ‎ ‎Earlier, the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, said President Tinubu’s directive was aimed at making agricultural inputs more affordable while strengthening domestic production and food security. ‎ ‎He disclosed that stakeholders had identified approximately 496,000 metric tonnes of fertiliser-related stocks, describing the quantity as a reasonable starting point for implementing the programme. ‎ ‎”From what has been presented, we have about 496,000 metric tonnes of stock, and it is a good, reasonable starting point,” the minister said. ‎ ‎Bagudu assured that the government would work with relevant stakeholders to identify additional funding opportunities through existing programmes to sustain the intervention beyond the immediate presidential directive. ‎ ‎”We will work with every other stakeholder to identify other government programmes that will have funding that can be used to support this initiative even beyond the duration of the President’s directive,” he stated. ‎ ‎Also speaking, the President of FEPSAN, Alhaji Abubakar Sadiq Kassim, commended President Tinubu for personally intervening to revive the country’s fertiliser industry. ‎ ‎”I want to thank the President for taking a personal interest in reviving the Nigerian fertiliser industry. We are extremely encouraged by this intervention because this is about food security, jobs, rural livelihoods and economic and social stability of our country,” he said. ‎ ‎Kassim noted that Nigeria had already made substantial investments in fertiliser blending plants, warehouses, distribution infrastructure and agro-dealer networks, but many of these facilities were operating below their installed capacity. ‎ ‎He explained that reviving the industry would not only increase fertiliser availability but also restore economic activities across production, transportation, storage and distribution networks. ‎ ‎According to him, FEPSAN members had completed an assessment of available NPK fertiliser stocks, raw materials and the industry’s capacity to produce additional quantities within the implementation period. ‎ ‎”Based on information received from our members, the raw materials currently available can support the production of about 148,000 metric tonnes of NPK 20-10-10 within the next few weeks as targeted. This will give about three million bags of fertiliser,” he disclosed. ‎ ‎The FEPSAN president further revealed that members were holding approximately 29,000 metric tonnes of finished NPK fertiliser that could be immediately purchased and released for distribution. ‎ ‎He expressed confidence that the industry had the capacity to make approximately 3.5 million bags of fertiliser available within the stipulated period, noting that existing stocks and blending facilities were spread across different parts of the country. ‎ ‎Kassim added that the geographical distribution of the facilities would support faster delivery and reduce the logistical burden of reaching farmers. ‎ ‎As part of the implementation framework, President Tinubu also approved the Bank of Agriculture (BOA) and the Bank of Industry (BOI) to serve as fund administrators and financial intermediaries for the initiative. ‎ ‎In a related presentation, a representative of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI) disclosed that the organisation had approximately 90,000 metric tonnes of materials on the ground, with additional goods in transit bringing the combined quantity to about 248,000 metric tonnes. The post Dry season farming: Shettima directs swift release of 3m fertiliser bags nationwide appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Wike to opposition: Stop creating chaos to blame Tinubu
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, yesterday, accused opposition political parties of deliberately fomenting trouble to make it appear that President Bola Tinubu is responsible for political violence ahead of the 2027 elections. Wike made the allegation during the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) in the FCT at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja. The minister, who expressed confidence in the APC’s chances in the upcoming elections, claimed that opposition parties knew they had already lost and were creating political tension to discredit the ruling party. Wike said: “You have what it takes to win this election. The other parties know. Let me just tell you the simple truth. The other parties know they have lost the election. “What are they doing now? What they are doing now is to foment crisis—foment problems to make it look as if it is the government; it is the presidential candidate of the APC party who is fomenting trouble. “They (opposition) are the ones causing trouble. You (APC PCC) don’t need to cause trouble because you have already won the election. “They (opposition parties) foment trouble and report as if they are not the ones that have created that problem. So, we must be on alert.” Wike also told members of the Rainbow Coalition to make sure the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, do not get 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT in the January 16, 2027 general elections. He warned the members against assuming the contest was already won, saying the election was a chance for the APC to show its political strength in the territory. On how to sell the president’s record, he said: “You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign.” Wike also dared opposition politicians to set projects built before 2023 beside those delivered since Tinubu took office, arguing that the work going on in the city centre and the satellite towns spoke for itself. item.title: 2027: APC rallies deepening Nigerians’ anger, Kawu warns party leaders
item.description: …Senator decries disconnect between northern masses and political elite, urges grassroots mobilisation By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Chairman of the Senate Committee on Petroleum (Downstream), Senator Kawu Sumaila Suleiman (APC, Kano South), has warned the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) that displays of opulence, celebrations and merrymaking at presidential campaign rallies are deepening the pains and anger of Nigerians. The senator, who is the APC senatorial candidate for the January 16, 2027 election, said there was a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between ordinary people in the North and the political elite. In a statement addressed to party leaders and members on Monday, his second intervention on the matter, Suleiman called for a change in the party’s approach and strategy ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged the APC leadership and Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) to prioritise effective communication of President Bola Tinubu’s policies and ongoing reforms to Nigerians at the grassroots. The lawmaker also called on the party to identify and empower credible individuals and stakeholders with genuine grassroots influence in their respective constituencies rather than relying on what he described as “Abuja politicians” and entitled individuals disconnected from the people. In the statement titled, “A Clarion Call for Self-Reflection, Humility, and Grassroots Reconnection”, Suleiman said the party’s message was still not reaching ordinary Nigerians. He said: “Following my earlier message, we must once again be completely honest with ourselves: our message is still not reaching the grassroots. We need to acknowledge and accept that there is a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between the common people in the North and the political elites. We must change our approach and strategy. “There is an urgent need to effectively communicate our government’s policies and the ongoing reforms of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu directly to the grassroots.” The senator warned that the celebratory atmosphere at campaign rallies was insensitive to the hardship and insecurity confronting many Nigerians, particularly in the North. He urged party leaders to remember victims of terrorism, thousands of Nigerians displaced from their communities and those forced to flee across the border into the Niger Republic. “The current displays of celebration, opulence, and pomp-dancing and merrymaking during presidential campaign rallies are only deepening the pains and anger of the citizens. “We must remember the countless people currently trapped in the hands of terrorists, the thousands suffering in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps, and those who have been forced to flee across the border into the Niger Republic,” he said. He urged the APC leadership and Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) to prioritise effective communication of President Bola Tinubu’s policies and ongoing reforms to Nigerians at the grassroots. The lawmaker also called on the party to identify and empower credible individuals and stakeholders with genuine grassroots influence in their respective constituencies rather than relying on what he described as “Abuja politicians” and entitled individuals disconnected from the people. In the statement titled, “A Clarion Call for Self-Reflection, Humility, and Grassroots Reconnection”, Suleiman said the party’s message was still not reaching ordinary Nigerians. He said: “Following my earlier message, we must once again be completely honest with ourselves: our message is still not reaching the grassroots. We need to acknowledge and accept that there is a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between the common people in the North and the political elites. We must change our approach and strategy. “There is an urgent need to effectively communicate our government’s policies and the ongoing reforms of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu directly to the grassroots.” The senator warned that the celebratory atmosphere at campaign rallies was insensitive to the hardship and insecurity confronting many Nigerians, particularly in the North. He urged party leaders to remember victims of terrorism, thousands of Nigerians displaced from their communities and those forced to flee across the border into the Niger Republic. “The current displays of celebration, opulence, and pomp-dancing and merrymaking during presidential campaign rallies are only deepening the pains and anger of the citizens. “We must remember the countless people currently trapped in the hands of terrorists, the thousands suffering in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps, and those who have been forced to flee across the border into the Niger Republic,” he said. Suleiman called for deep reflection among APC leaders, reminding them of the responsibility entrusted to them by Tinubu. “It is time for deep self-reflection. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has entrusted us with a sacred responsibility (Amana), and we must protect and honour it,” he said. Acknowledging that his message might offend some party leaders, the senator said genuine loyalty required speaking honestly about issues affecting the party’s collective interest. He also cautioned against sycophancy and selfish political ambitions, urging party members to place the country’s stability and the party’s success above personal interests. Suleiman prayed for Tinubu’s continued success, victory for APC candidates in the forthcoming elections and lasting peace and security across Nigeria. item.title: Live: Russian attacks target bridges in Kyiv, knocking out heating and water
item.description: Russian strikes hit two major bridges in Kyiv late Monday, part of an overnight attack that damaged critical infrastructure and disrupted heating and water in parts of the capital, its mayor said. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of an attack by Russia in the coming days even as negotiators representing Kyiv as well as Europe and the United States held talks on future negotiations with Russia aimed at finding a path to end the war.

item.title: Don’t turn churches into campaign arena, Soludo cautions politicians
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State, on Sunday, cautioned politicians against turning churches and other places of worship into a political arena, stating that sacred spaces must remain neutral grounds for people of all political persuasions. Soludo made the remark during the 30th anniversary celebration of the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. Addressing the congregation, the governor stressed the need for the men of God to clearly separate politics from worship. According to Soludo, the place of worship should be a holy place where people of all political persuasion should come and worship God in peace. “It should not be a place for politics. There is a venue for politics. If you want to worship God, you have to go to the house of God. We must separate the two things clearly,” Soludo said. He recalled that six months before his election, he took a deliberate decision never to go to any church to cup a microphone to ask them to vote for him or to campaign. “It was a deliberate decision. I worshipped in the government house chapel until the election day and afterwards,” the governor stated. “We must never politicise the church. We must never politicise the place of worship. Politicians, keep off churches. Keep off places of worship. That’s a deliberate message, and it is my kind of consistency of character”, he further said. item.title: US extends chip sale restrictions to more Asian countries to reduce risk of ‘diversion’ to China
item.description: The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has decided to ban remote access to certain GPUs and servers running in datacenters located in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. The agency has also introduced a requirement to secure a license before selling what it describes as “advanced super intelligence (SI) chips and servers” that are sufficiently powerful to “be used for training or running of advanced SI models” into the five nations. The interim final rule [PDF] containing the new regulations says they’re needed “to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on US technology to threaten US national security and foreign policy interests.” Similar language can be found in previous US bans on sales of GPUs and other advanced tech to China, which Washington fears will use advanced tech to improve its military capabilities. US authorities understood that export bans wouldn’t prevent Chinese entities from renting GPUs housed elsewhere. So from 2021 to 2024, Washington introduced a series of regulations that required US-based clouds to make sure they didn’t serve Chinese customers. No such obligation existed for cloud operators elsewhere, which created a market for resources that Chinese customers could access from afar. It is widely felt that datacenter building booms in Malaysia and Thailand, both of which are generally on good terms with China, aimed to cater to Middle Kingdom customers who wanted to rent GPUs they could not import. Megapseed – whose former employee Alice Huang had an intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and may have been a Chinese intelligence asset – built datacenters in Malaysia and was suspected of catering largely to offshore customers. Neil Shah, vice president of research at analyst firm Counterpoint, said the new rules shift the regulatory burden of complying with export controls from hardware manufacturers to cloud operators. “Data center operators in hubs such as Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia will now face massive ‘Know Your Customer's Workload’ requirements,” he told The Register by email, likening it to the KYC restrictions imposed on financial services firms. “They must prove to US regulators that their compute is not being funneled back to embargoed nations, or risk losing their own access to US silicon.” He feels the new rules represent “a severe short-term compute bottleneck for Chinese tech giants” and “a massive long-term catalyst for decoupling.” “Washington is forcing domestic capital and engineering talent to double down on full-stack sovereign alternatives, accelerating ecosystems like Huawei's Ascend.” Shah’s observation came days after Alibaba decided to spin out its T-Head chip design unit, which it described as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China.” That description suggests Alibaba doesn’t think T-Head has strong prospects of selling its

Megapseed – whose former employee Alice Huang had an intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and may have been a Chinese intelligence asset – built datacenters in Malaysia and was suspected of catering largely to offshore customers. Neil Shah, vice president of research at analyst firm Counterpoint, said the new rules shift the regulatory burden of complying with export controls from hardware manufacturers to cloud operators. “Data center operators in hubs such as Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia will now face massive ‘Know Your Customer's Workload’ requirements,” he told The Register by email, likening it to the KYC restrictions imposed on financial services firms. “They must prove to US regulators that their compute is not being funneled back to embargoed nations, or risk losing their own access to US silicon.” He feels the new rules represent “a severe short-term compute bottleneck for Chinese tech giants” and “a massive long-term catalyst for decoupling.” “Washington is forcing domestic capital and engineering talent to double down on full-stack sovereign alternatives, accelerating ecosystems like Huawei's Ascend.” Shah’s observation came days after Alibaba decided to spin out its T-Head chip design unit, which it described as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China.” That description suggests Alibaba doesn’t think T-Head has strong prospects of selling its wares outside China. It remains to be seen if the new BIS rules will slow datacenter development across Asia and Brazil. All five nations the US has regulated are all enjoying the economic impact of the AI boom. They’re also trying to manage its impact. Singapore limits datacenter construction, as befits a tiny and resource-constrained island nation. Malaysia is very much open for business but has introduced increasingly strict building codes and requirements to minimize energy and water consumption. Thailand recently introduced new regulations that new builds of large datacenters must take place in designated industrial zones. Indonesia also has strong regulations but is not currently a major datacenter hub. Brazil requires datacenter operators to reserve at least 10 percent of capacity for local users, suggesting some operators are more interested in offshore customers. Interestingly, the new BIS rules don’t impact infrastructure used for “commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat.” Chinese e-tailers operate at vast scale and have already attracted regulatory attention in Europe and the USA. Asian and Brazilian datacenter operators therefore probably do not see the likes of Temu and Alibaba as a lifeline, but might see a role as regional hosts for outfits like Amazon or Meta. ®

item.title: Obi, Kwankwaso have God’s grace to dislodge Tinubu — Babachir Lawal
item.description: A chieftain of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Babachir Lawal, has said Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Kwankwaso, his running mate, have God’s backing to defeat President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Lawal, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, who made the declaration during an appearance on Arise Television late Sunday, cited the “widespread support” Obi and Kwankwaso enjoyed as a pointer to God’s grace upon their lives. He said: “I have told everybody that talks to me that both Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have the grace of God upon their lives, which makes people like them. “The population likes them. They just show up in the market. They don’t hire people to come to their rallies. People just turn out at their own expense.” He said his experience in politics had enabled him to recognise signs that could favour the opposition alliance, adding that he previously occupied a similar position during the Muhammadu Buhari administration. “It’s not the first time I am in the position I am in now in politics. I have been in this position during Buhari’s time. Even this your president, I drove his system up to the primaries. “So I am a very skilled and experienced person in the game. I can see the signs and we know the loopholes. And we are working on the loopholes,’’ he said. Lawal expressed confidence that the NDC would defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. , saying the party had established structures and systems to achieve its objective. “We have an inside chance of toppling this government. We are inside and we know we will beat this government. “We know they are gone. We have put up structures and systems. I am 100 per cent confident,’’ he said. Lawal added that the responsibility of the party’s technical team was to convert the popularity of its presidential candidates into electoral success by ensuring that votes were protected and counted. “This grace that God has bestowed upon them, it’s our duty, the technical people, to harmonise and crystallise this thing into delivering it at the polling station and protecting the votes and ensuring it’s counted,” he said. Lawal dismissed concerns over recent departure of Yunusa Tanko, former national coordinator of the Obidient Movement; Nana Kazaure, Doyin Okupe, and the former NDC’s deputy national publicity secretary, from Obi’s camp, saying politicians were free to leave parties when their expectations were not met. He compared the development with the exit of some politicians from Tinubu’s inner circle, including Kashim Imam and Rauf Aregbesola. “I was with Bola Tinubu, but I left. I can remember Kashim Imam; he has also left. I remember Rauf Aregbesola, who was also with Bola Tinubu. But he has left. These are big politicians. But they left Bola Tinubu. “Leaving a political party is only natural. Nigeria is like a big company with many political parties. item.title: California sues OpenAI for misleading public about AI safety
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has sued OpenAI under the state's unfair competition and public nuisance laws, for allegedly misleading and endangering the public by deploying unsafe AI models. The lawsuit [PDF], filed in California Superior Court, follows the compromise of Hugging Face's infrastructure and other cyber incidents OpenAI's experimental models caused when taking autonomous actions without authorization or supervision. "While narratives about the Hugging Face attack have evoked science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok, let me be clear: the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents," said Attorney General Bonta. At a press conference , Bonta added: "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public." The legal salvo comes after Bonta in September sent OpenAI a letter seeking information about these agentic attacks. According to the complaint, "OpenAI failed to substantially comply" with the investigatory subpoena. In August, 15 states led by Iowa – and excluding California – issued a joint demand for OpenAI to provide information about how its models hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. Bonta's office previously joined with Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings to urge OpenAI to do more for children's safety in light of reports that its models produced sexually inappropriate output. California did not, however, join the eight states that sued OpenAI in October over alleged misrepresentations about child safety. Florida and Texas have also made child safety claims. Child safety plays well politically; California appears to be the first state to demand more accountability toward the general public. Bonta's lawsuit, in a state that has largely accommodated the AI industry for the sake of economic benefits and political contributions , suggests that California officials may be more willing to bite the hand that feeds. The many Democratic victories in the US midterm elections may also be a factor, as pundits feel voters swung to give lawmakers license to regulate the unpopular AI industry. At his press conference, Bonta made sure to convey that he wants accountability without smothering the AI industry in costly regulation. "Let me be clear," he said. "I believe in the technological and economic power of AI. If we're able to address these very high stakes safety issues, AI could lead to some of the most incredible improvements in the history of humankind." AI is yet to deliver those incredible improvements. It has delivered deepfakes, huge quantities of cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and the permissionless resale of past intellectual labor, plus high energy and RAM prices. As well as some productivity gains

At a press conference , Bonta added: "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public." The legal salvo comes after Bonta in September sent OpenAI a letter seeking information about these agentic attacks. According to the complaint, "OpenAI failed to substantially comply" with the investigatory subpoena. In August, 15 states led by Iowa – and excluding California – issued a joint demand for OpenAI to provide information about how its models hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. Bonta's office previously joined with Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings to urge OpenAI to do more for children's safety in light of reports that its models produced sexually inappropriate output. California did not, however, join the eight states that sued OpenAI in October over alleged misrepresentations about child safety. Florida and Texas have also made child safety claims. Child safety plays well politically; California appears to be the first state to demand more accountability toward the general public. Bonta's lawsuit, in a state that has largely accommodated the AI industry for the sake of economic benefits and political contributions , suggests that California officials may be more willing to bite the hand that feeds. The many Democratic victories in the US midterm elections may also be a factor, as pundits feel voters swung to give lawmakers license to regulate the unpopular AI industry. At his press conference, Bonta made sure to convey that he wants accountability without smothering the AI industry in costly regulation. "Let me be clear," he said. "I believe in the technological and economic power of AI. If we're able to address these very high stakes safety issues, AI could lead to some of the most incredible improvements in the history of humankind." AI is yet to deliver those incredible improvements. It has delivered deepfakes, huge quantities of cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and the permissionless resale of past intellectual labor, plus high energy and RAM prices. As well as some productivity gains in certain areas like coding, albeit at an unknown cost to future job markets. But as AI boosters insist, miracle drugs and endless vacations aren't far off … perhaps along with existential crises. Katharine Trendacosta, director of policy and advocacy at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, told The Register in an email that the EFF is glad to see state officials taking action against AI companies taking unreasonable risks with public safety. "Several recent cybersecurity incidents at AI labs could have been prevented or substantially mitigated by adhering to longstanding cybersecurity best practices, such as proper sandboxing, monitoring, and logging," said Trendacosta. "AI agents can be useful tools when deployed appropriately, with adequate safeguards designed to mitigate the risks. Companies should carefully consider the risks of every use case, including the consequences, reversibility, and sensitivity of any action an agent is used for." ®
