item.title: Gombe approves N97bn road projects, N3.8bn emergency vehicles
item.description: …SEC endorses 2027–2029 expenditure framework, updates social protection policy .. Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state. The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion. Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Moses Kyari Bolda, said the decisions reflected the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, improved public services and long-term economic growth. On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas. Among the approved projects is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months. Similarly, the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak, was awarded to EEC International Limited at N49.3 billion, also with a 24-month completion period. The council also approved the first phase of the Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road project, covering approximately 15 kilometres, to be executed by EEC International Limited at N26.3 billion. Other projects include the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road, covering Degri to Sikam, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at approximately N4 billion. The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited. The seventh project, covering 1.5 kilometres of the Kunuwal Road Network, was awarded to Swas Grade Limited. Abdullahi explained that the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road would be implemented in phases, with the initial four-kilometre stretch from Degri to Sikam approved as the first phase. item.content:encoded: …SEC endorses 2027–2029 expenditure framework, updates social protection policy .. Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state. The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion. Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Moses Kyari Bolda, said the decisions reflected the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, improved public services and long-term economic growth. On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas. Among the approved projects is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months. Similarly, the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak, was awarded to EEC International Limited at N49.3 billion, also with a 24-month completion period. The council also approved the first phase of the Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road project, covering approximately 15 kilometres, to be executed by EEC International Limited at N26.3 billion. Other projects include the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road, covering Degri to Sikam, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at approximately N4 billion. The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited. The seventh project, covering 1.5 kilometres of the Kunuwal Road Network, was awarded to Swas Grade Limited. Abdullahi explained that the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road would be implemented in phases, with the initial four-kilometre stretch from Degri to Sikam approved as the first phase. He described the approvals as an expansion of the state’s infrastructure development programme, particularly the administration’s Network 1,100 Kilometres Road Initiative, designed to open up rural communities, improve access to markets and facilitate the movement of people, goods and services. He added that the projects would strengthen inter-community connectivity, promote agricultural and commercial activities and improve access to essential public services. Governor Yahaya, he said, was expected to perform the foundation-laying ceremony for the Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including the Dalawaja spur, to formally signal the commencement of construction. N3.8bn for emergency vehicles In another development, the council approved the procurement of 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers at a combined cost of approximately N3.8 billion. The Commissioner for Finance, Muhammad Gambo Magaji, said the acquisition of the firefighting trucks would strengthen the operational capacity of the State Fire Service, particularly as the government expands fire service stations beyond the state capital. He explained that the additional water tankers would provide temporary relief to residents while the ongoing revitalisation of the Gombe Regional Water Supply Scheme was being completed, including plans to transition its operations to solar-powered energy. Magaji disclosed that all 40 vehicles would be converted from diesel-powered engines to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) to reduce fuel expenditure, improve operational efficiency and promote cleaner energy. Kolmani oil exploration Meanwhile, the state government said it had intensified preparations to position Gombe for the anticipated resumption of oil exploration activities in the Kolmani area, with drilling expected to resume in the first week of December 2026. The Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Sanusi Ahmad Pindiga, said the government was working with Rift Oil Nigeria Limited, a consultant engaged to facilitate the state’s institutional engagement, recognition and registration as an oil and gas-producing state. He disclosed that the consultant had completed 12 of its 14 planned deliverables, representing significant progress in developing the institutional framework and human capital required for the state’s participation in the oil and gas industry. One of the major achievements, according to him, was the training of 100 graduates in artisan skills, including plumbing, carpentry, information and communication technology and welding. The beneficiaries were also provided with starter kits and financial support to enable them establish businesses, become self-reliant and position themselves for employment and entrepreneurial opportunities arising from the anticipated expansion of oil and gas activities. Pindiga said the consultant’s engagements had also facilitated the preparation of relevant documentation and institutional support mechanisms considered necessary for the state’s participation in the emerging petroleum industry. He described the expected resumption of drilling in Kolmani as a significant economic opportunity, stressing the need to prepare the state’s institutions, workforce and communities to benefit from the development. SEC approves 2027–2029 fiscal framework In another major decision, the council approved the Gombe State Medium-Term Expenditure Framework for 2027–2029, which will provide the fiscal and economic projections guiding revenue generation and expenditure priorities over the next three years. The Commissioner for Budget, Micah Sunday Hamman, said the framework would serve as the foundation for preparing the 2027 budget while strengthening fiscal discipline, resource allocation and effective implementation of government programmes. He explained that the MTEF would provide a realistic basis for projecting revenue and expenditure, ensuring that government policies, projects and programmes were aligned with available resources and clearly defined development priorities. The council also approved an updated Gombe State Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 to strengthen the state’s social welfare system and provide coordinated and sustainable support for vulnerable and disadvantaged citizens. According to Hamman, the policy would consolidate existing government interventions and establish a comprehensive framework for protecting vulnerable groups, particularly children and other citizens requiring social assistance. He identified the five pillars of the policy as social assistance, social insurance, labour market interventions, systems strengthening, and protection against discrimination, violence, exploitation and social exclusion. The commissioner said the framework would emphasise transparency, inclusion and evidence-based implementation to ensure that social protection interventions reached their intended beneficiaries and improved their living conditions. The latest decisions, he added, underscored the state government’s determination to combine infrastructure expansion with sound fiscal management, improved emergency services, social welfare and strategic economic planning as Gombe prepares for its next phase of development. item.title: Swansea braced to lose Vítor Matos as Strasbourg seek to replace Hugo Oliveira
item.description: Matos has indicated a desire for move to Ligue 1 Championship club would be due compensation Swansea City are increasingly resigned to their head coach, Vítor Matos, joining Strasbourg after he indicated a desire to join Chelsea’s sister club. The Ligue 1 club have approached Swansea with a view to Matos succeeding Hugo Oliveira. Strasbourg, acquired by Chelsea’s parent company BlueCo in 2023, have identified Matos as a replacement for Oliveira, who has won three of 10 league matches since succeeding Gary O’Neil in July. The French club are hovering two points above the relegation zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Mimiko congratulates Aiyedatiwa on Silverbird award
item.description: …Urges Ondo governor to deepen dividends of democracy By Dayo Johnson, Akure Former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has congratulated Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa on emerging as the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year. Mimiko described the award as recognition of the achievements recorded so far by the Aiyedatiwa administration and its efforts towards developing the state. The award was presented at the 20th edition of the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards held at Eko Hotels, Lagos. In a congratulatory message, the former governor urged Aiyedatiwa to see the recognition as a call to do more for the people of Ondo State and deepen the dividends of democracy. He said the honour by the Silverbird Group showed that the governor’s efforts were receiving recognition beyond the state. “This honour from the Silverbird Group is an acknowledgement that your efforts are being noticed and should, therefore, spur you to do more for the benefit of the greater majority of our compatriots in our dear state,” Mimiko said. He described Ondo State’s selection for the award among the 36 states as encouraging, noting that it reflected efforts being made across different sectors and communities. “It is encouraging to see Ondo State singled out among the 36 states for this award. It speaks to some work being done across sectors and locations in the state,” he added. Mimiko prayed for greater strength and wisdom for Aiyedatiwa as he continues to steer the affairs of the state. item.title: Anambra Patriots endorse APGA-APC alliance, adopt Tinubu for 2027
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A political pressure group in Anambra State, Anambra Patriots, APS, has endorsed the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, and the All Progressives Congress, APC, adopting President Bola Tinubu as its preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election. The group also declared its support for the re-election of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, and urged Ndigbo to support his political direction, including his backing for Tinubu. The convener of APS and Anambra State Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, disclosed the group’s position on Sunday during the Anambra Patriots Women Summit held in Awka, the state capital. Ezeobi expressed dissatisfaction with those criticising Soludo for aligning politically with Tinubu rather than supporting former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi. He argued that politics should be driven by interests rather than sentiments, insisting that Soludo’s decision to support Tinubu was in the interest of Ndigbo. “My problem with Ndigbo is that they don’t know how to play politics. We do politics of emotion instead of interest. In politics, you get what you contributed, not what you deserve. Politics is about interest,” he said. According to him, Soludo’s support for Tinubu was not motivated by personal gains but by what he described as the need for greater political inclusion of the South-East in national affairs. He said: “Prof. Soludo’s support for Tinubu is not for personal gain, but for the interest of Ndigbo. It is time for Ndigbo to come back to Nigeria. And Soludo is a professor; he has analysed Nigerian politics.” Ezeobi also argued that Soludo should not be criticised for his political choice, saying other ethnic groups had members supporting Obi without attracting similar criticism. Ezeobi, however, maintained that Soludo had not insulted Obi but had only responded to comments he considered critical of Anambra State and APGA. He further criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, describing it as the political platform of a Bayelsa politician, while questioning Obi’s influence within the party. The commissioner said the APS had resolved to support Tinubu in the presidential election while backing APGA candidates in other electoral contests. “Today, we are adopting President Tinubu as the candidate to support in the 2027 presidential election, and we have approved Governor Soludo-led APGA and Tinubu’s APC. We will vote APC in the presidential election and vote APGA in other elections,” he declared. Also speaking, the Secretary to the Anambra State Government, Lady Chiamaka Nnake, a founding member of APS, urged residents to join Soludo in supporting Tinubu. Similarly, the Chairman of APS, Ozoh Ejiamatu Damian Enekwechi, urged the people of the state to follow Soludo’s political direction. “We are only following our leader. That is what we are doing. item.title: True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni
item.description: … Backs YASA Foundation’s drive for inclusive society By Ogochukwu Agha lagos—The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has urged Nigerians, corporate organisations and philanthropists to support initiatives that empower vulnerable people, saying true fulfilment lies in making positive impact on others. The monarch spoke at the unveiling of the Yeye Afolashade Shona-Aluko (YASA) Foundation in Lagos, where he donated N5 million. Describing the foundation’s humanitarian mission as worthy of support, Oba Ogunwusi said: “What gives the greatest happiness in this world is a life of impact and fulfilment. Everybody is chasing money. But when you attain a certain level of wealth, you discover that money does not necessarily bring happiness. “The essence of life is what you can give to others.” Senator Sylvia Mthethwa of Eswatini urged governments and institutions to promote inclusive development, asking: “Are we developing societies in which everybody has an opportunity to participate or contribute and prosper?” She called for improved access to education, healthcare and employment for persons with disabilities. The Ooni’s wife, Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi, commended the foundation’s founder, urging her to remain committed to humanitarian service despite challenges. Earlier, Shona-Aluko said her youngest son’s disability inspired her intervention. She recalled employing eight specialised teachers to support him and other children at Ikeja High School for about nine years. She said the experience exposed the difficulties faced by families unable to afford specialised education. “YASA Foundation was born from a burden… a burden to give voice to the voiceless, strength to the weak, and to say boldly: ‘You are not forgotten,’” she said. The foundation focuses on inclusive education, healthcare, rehabilitation, assistive devices, vocational training and livelihood support. The event featured beneficiaries’ testimonies and recognition of Shona-Aluko by two international institutions. The post True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated. Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks. Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations. Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system. She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival. “The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care. “However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said. She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified. Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays. “The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. item.content:encoded: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated. Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks. Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations. Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system. She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival. “The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care. “However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said. She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified. Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays. “The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. As a result, valuable time is wasted accessing the wrong care when the patient could have been connected to the right facility through a coordinated system,” she added. Atanda, who co-founded an ambulance service provider and subsequently developed technology for coordinating emergency services, said her organisation had also extended its activities to intensive care and surgical services through TAC Care at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH. She said the objective was to demonstrate how an integrated emergency response model could work and encourage governments to adopt and strengthen similar arrangements. On complaints about unanswered emergency calls and delayed ambulance response, Atanda said a properly coordinated system must guarantee round-the-clock communication and effective dispatch of emergency services. “We operate a 24-hour communication centre where someone is available to receive calls, establish the caller’s location and coordinate assistance. The goal is to ensure that patients receive the support they need throughout their emergency care journey,” she said. She added that private sector initiatives could demonstrate workable models that government agencies could subsequently integrate into the national emergency response framework. On the cost of emergency treatment, Atanda acknowledged that quality healthcare remained expensive but argued that health insurance offered one of the most sustainable ways of reducing the financial burden on patients and their families. “We cannot continue to rely on out-of-pocket payments for every healthcare emergency. It is simply not sustainable,” she said. Beyond insurance, Atanda called for stronger government-private sector partnerships, noting that the government had the authority to formulate policies and wider community reach, while private organisations could contribute operational expertise and service delivery capacity. “There should be policies that make health insurance compulsory, while the government can also pool resources and allocate funds specifically for emergency care, “The faster a patient accesses appropriate care, the better the chances of survival and recovery. If it takes days before someone receives treatment, the likelihood of a positive outcome becomes significantly lower,” she said. The emergency care advocate also called for stronger public preparedness, saying Nigerians needed to understand how to recognise emergencies, seek assistance and provide basic first aid before professional responders arrived. She said public education and first aid training were essential because emergency responders might not reach victims immediately after an incident. “When you call for help, it may take at least five minutes for emergency responders to reach you. What do you do during those minutes before help arrives?” she asked. She urged Nigerians to acquire basic skills to recognise conditions such as seizures and strokes, understand the appropriate response and provide accurate information when contacting emergency services. Atanda said her ambulance company provided first aid training for individuals, corporate organisations and healthcare professionals, but stressed the need to expand such programmes and make emergency preparedness part of everyday life. “We need to make emergency response information part of our everyday lives so that people understand how to seek help when emergencies occur,” she said. She maintained that building a functional emergency care system would require sustained collaboration, public education, accessible health insurance and a reliable network capable of connecting patients to appropriate care without unnecessary delays The post Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 67th NCH: Nasarawa seeks actionable resolutions to improve healthcare delivery
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Nasarawa State Government has called on health sector leaders across the country to translate commitments and policy decisions into measurable outcomes that will improve healthcare delivery, particularly at the grassroots. The Governor of the State, Abdullahi Sule, made the call on Monday while declaring open the Technical Session of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, the state capital. This was contained in a statement signed by the Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ado Bako. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Akabe, Sule said the Council provided an important platform for stakeholders to develop practical solutions to the challenges confronting Nigeria’s health sector. He expressed confidence that deliberations under the theme, “From Commitments to Results: Delivering Quality and Equitable Healthcare for All Nigerians,” would produce actionable recommendations to strengthen the country’s healthcare system. The Governor described Nasarawa’s selection as host of the national meeting as a privilege and an opportunity to showcase the state’s peaceful environment, hospitality and economic potential. He also reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting national health sector reforms and ensuring a successful meeting. He urged delegates to take advantage of the state’s hospitality during their stay. Earlier, the Nasarawa state Commissioner for Health, Dr. Gwamna Gaza, described the meeting as a historic opportunity for the state to host health sector leaders from across the country for the first time. He stressed that decisions reached at the Council would have far-reaching implications for the country’s health sector, urging participants to remain conscious of the fact that they were also beneficiaries of the policies and reforms being formulated for Nigerians. He also called for active participation and constructive contributions, assuring delegates that the state government and relevant institutions were available to address any challenges they might encounter during the meeting. He urged delegates to take advantage of the state’s hospitality during their stay. Earlier, the Nasarawa state Commissioner for Health, Dr. Gwamna Gaza, described the meeting as a historic opportunity for the state to host health sector leaders from across the country for the first time. Presenting the procedures for the Technical Session, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and Chairman of the Technical Committee, Daju Kachollom, said the two-day meeting, scheduled for November 16 and 17, would provide the technical foundation for the main Council meeting on November 19 and 20. She explained that the main Council meeting would be chaired by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate. Kachollom, said the memoranda submitted for consideration were organised around the four pillars of the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint. The pillars, she listed, were effective governance; efficient, equitable and quality health systems; unlocking value chains; and health security. She said the submissions would address critical areas, including the implementation of the National Health Act, multisectoral health interventions, clinical research and development, as well as strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to detect, prevent and respond to public health threats. These threats, she noted, included cholera, Lassa fever, cerebrospinal meningitis and measles. To ensure focused deliberations, the Permanent Secretary said summaries of the memoranda had been prepared as working documents, while authors would be given five minutes each to present their submissions, highlight key issues and outline recommendations. “The Secretariat will subsequently consolidate the Technical Committee’s recommendations for consideration by the Council,” she said. She also disclosed that the Ministry had adopted an electronic documentation system for the Council, with relevant meeting documents preloaded onto tablets provided to participants. item.title: Perseverance Update: The Ghostly Rocks of ‘Idubi’ — Bright Remnants of Aqueous Systems from Long Ago
item.description: Explore This Section Perseverance Home Mission Overview Rover Components Mars Rock Samples Where is Perseverance? Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Mission Updates Science Overview Objectives Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Perseverance Raw Images Images Videos Audio More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 2 min read Perseverance Update: The Ghostly Rocks of ‘Idubi’ — Bright Remnants of Aqueous Systems from Long Ago NASA’s Perseverance rover captured this image of a bright, silica-rich rock in the “Idubi” area using its left Mastcam-Z camera on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023) at the local mean solar time of 13:03:53. NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU Written by Candice Bedford, Research Scientist at Purdue University Date: Nov. 16, 2026 During the Perseverance rover’s investigation of “Idubi” — an area of ancient Martian crust exposed in the “Lac de Charmes” region, outside of Jezero crater — the Perseverance rover team has been captivated by a cluster of eerily bright, light-toned rocks in the area. These bright fragments stand out sharply against the underlying darker and often dust-covered Martian surface, and are even brighter than the igneous and impactite rocks we previously investigated. Suspecting that they differed from the typical igneous rocks in the area, the rover team directed Perseverance to investigate. Newly downlinked data from the SuperCam instrument has confirmed that these light-toned rocks are not igneous in origin and instead are rich in hydrated silica. Hydrated silica can form in many aqueous environments on the Earth, including hydrothermal, pedogenic, and groundwater systems. As such, these types of deposits are prime targets for understanding Mars’ hydrological history, as several of these environments could have been capable of supporting life. Furthermore, hydrated silica holds immense astrobiological value due to its remarkable capacity to preserve microfossils. Could these pale remnants of an ancient Martian water system hold signs of ancient life? When Perseverance previously encountered silica-rich rocks on the inner rim of Jezero Crater, the deposits were too small to deploy proximity science instruments and gather the high-resolution chemical and mineralogical data needed to constrain their origin and biosignature preservation potential. Fortunately, the rocks at “Idubi” offer a much more promising scale, and a detailed proximity science campaign is already underway. A close-up image of a silica-rich rock in the “Idubi” area using the Perseverance rover’s SHERLOC WATSON camera, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm. This image was acquired on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023) at the local mean solar time of 17:33:55. NASA/JPL-Caltech Want to read more posts from the Perseverance team? Visit Mission Updates Want to learn more about Perseverance’s science instruments? Visit the Science In

Suspecting that they differed from the typical igneous rocks in the area, the rover team directed Perseverance to investigate. Newly downlinked data from the SuperCam instrument has confirmed that these light-toned rocks are not igneous in origin and instead are rich in hydrated silica. Hydrated silica can form in many aqueous environments on the Earth, including hydrothermal, pedogenic, and groundwater systems. As such, these types of deposits are prime targets for understanding Mars’ hydrological history, as several of these environments could have been capable of supporting life. Furthermore, hydrated silica holds immense astrobiological value due to its remarkable capacity to preserve microfossils. Could these pale remnants of an ancient Martian water system hold signs of ancient life? When Perseverance previously encountered silica-rich rocks on the inner rim of Jezero Crater, the deposits were too small to deploy proximity science instruments and gather the high-resolution chemical and mineralogical data needed to constrain their origin and biosignature preservation potential. Fortunately, the rocks at “Idubi” offer a much more promising scale, and a detailed proximity science campaign is already underway. A close-up image of a silica-rich rock in the “Idubi” area using the Perseverance rover’s SHERLOC WATSON camera, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm. This image was acquired on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023) at the local mean solar time of 17:33:55. NASA/JPL-Caltech Want to read more posts from the Perseverance team? item.title: Drug insecurity threatens national security, pharmacists warn FG
item.description: … Seeks 1% of seized drug trafficking assets to fund enforcement … Demands government control of medicine supply chain By Chioma Obinna The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a serious threat to Nigeria’s national security, urging the Federal Government to strengthen regulatory control of medicines and prevent the transfer of critical drug management responsibilities from public authorities to private interests. The society also called for the establishment of a special fund to tackle illicit financial flows in the healthcare sector, proposing that one per cent of assets seized from drug trafficking be dedicated to strengthening the enforcement activities of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged IJELE 2026, held from November 2 to 7 at the International Convention Centre, Awka, Anambra State. The conference, which brought together pharmacists and other stakeholders in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors, was held under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.” In the communiqué signed by the President, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba, and National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehin, the pharmacists maintained that medicines were not merely commercial commodities but matters of permanent regulatory control and national security. Citing Part I, Item 21 of the Second Schedule of the 1999 Constitution, the conference argued that the government’s responsibility for drug regulation and control could not be compromised by private-sector participation in the pharmaceutical supply chain. It cautioned against what it described as a private takeover of drug distribution responsibilities at the public-sector level, warning that such an arrangement could weaken inter-agency collaboration among the PCN, NAFDAC and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA). The communiqué stated: “Conference reminded Government that drugs are a matter of permanent regulatory control and National Security, which is why it is listed as Part I item 21, in the 2nd Schedule of the 1999 Constitution.” It added that while government could engage private-sector expertise in financing and technology deployment, it should not surrender its regulatory standing or the cooperation currently extended by relevant agencies to Federal Central Medical Stores and Federal Health Institutions. The PSN further called for the integration of community pharmacies into Nigeria’s national security architecture and the Nigeria Health Insurance Authority’s proposed Pharmacy First initiative. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: … Seeks 1% of seized drug trafficking assets to fund enforcement … Demands government control of medicine supply chain By Chioma Obinna The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a serious threat to Nigeria’s national security, urging the Federal Government to strengthen regulatory control of medicines and prevent the transfer of critical drug management responsibilities from public authorities to private interests. The society also called for the establishment of a special fund to tackle illicit financial flows in the healthcare sector, proposing that one per cent of assets seized from drug trafficking be dedicated to strengthening the enforcement activities of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged IJELE 2026, held from November 2 to 7 at the International Convention Centre, Awka, Anambra State. The conference, which brought together pharmacists and other stakeholders in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors, was held under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.” In the communiqué signed by the President, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba, and National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehin, the pharmacists maintained that medicines were not merely commercial commodities but matters of permanent regulatory control and national security. Citing Part I, Item 21 of the Second Schedule of the 1999 Constitution, the conference argued that the government’s responsibility for drug regulation and control could not be compromised by private-sector participation in the pharmaceutical supply chain. It cautioned against what it described as a private takeover of drug distribution responsibilities at the public-sector level, warning that such an arrangement could weaken inter-agency collaboration among the PCN, NAFDAC and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA). The communiqué stated: “Conference reminded Government that drugs are a matter of permanent regulatory control and National Security, which is why it is listed as Part I item 21, in the 2nd Schedule of the 1999 Constitution.” It added that while government could engage private-sector expertise in financing and technology deployment, it should not surrender its regulatory standing or the cooperation currently extended by relevant agencies to Federal Central Medical Stores and Federal Health Institutions. The PSN further called for the integration of community pharmacies into Nigeria’s national security architecture and the Nigeria Health Insurance Authority’s proposed Pharmacy First initiative. According to the conference, more than 10,000 community pharmacies across the country could serve as frontline health and security stakeholders by identifying and reporting suspicious drug-related activities. The pharmacists also urged the Federal Government to support the Drug Revolving Fund and Federal Drug Management Agency Bill, which has passed its first reading at the House of Representatives. They proposed that the agency should serve as a single purchasing and supply platform for medicines, while government pharmacists should retain responsibility for procurement decisions, quality assurance, storage, dispensing and the handling of controlled medicines in the civil service. On the existing Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Ministry of Health and Medipool, the conference called for a review to limit private-sector participation to pooled price negotiations or competitively selected framework suppliers on a non-exclusive basis, in line with the Procurement Act. To drive the proposed reforms, the PSN recommended a Federal Government-initiated Independent Presidential Committee on the Pharmaceutical Sector, to be chaired by a registered pharmacist recommended by the society, with representation from the PCN, NAFDAC, the National Institute for Pharmaceutical Research and Development and the PSN. The conference called for greater involvement of pharmacists in humanitarian operations, particularly in emergencies and situations involving displacement. It noted that humanitarian crises frequently disrupt access to essential medicines and healthcare services, leaving displaced persons, especially those living with chronic conditions, vulnerable to interruptions in treatment. The conference urged the development of a stronger humanitarian pharmacy workforce equipped to support medicine supply systems, maintain access to essential medicines, assist in chronic disease management and provide pharmaceutical care in emergency settings. It said pharmacists’ expertise in medicine selection, storage, supply, dispensing and appropriate use should be better integrated into national humanitarian preparedness and response plans. On the broader health sector, the pharmacists warned that Nigeria could not achieve meaningful national development while citizens remained frequently ill, essential medicines were inaccessible and health institutions operated in isolation. They identified five strategic bridges needed to transform the country’s health system: implementation, financing, medicine sovereignty, integration and accountability. The conference stressed the need for connected knowledge, coordinated professional practice, coherent policies and accountable leadership, urging government to translate policy commitments into measurable outcomes and lasting health impact. It also applauded the collaboration between the PSN and the West African Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (WASPEN), calling for a standardised framework to improve workforce planning and integrate advanced pharmacists into multidisciplinary clinical teams. The conference welcomed the harmonisation of the PSN-WASPEN initiative with the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria’s mandatory continuing professional development training modules. On workers’ welfare, the PSN commended the Nigeria Labour Congress, Trade Union Congress and the Joint Health Sector Unions/Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations for sustaining the struggle for justice and equity in the health sector. It appealed to the labour centres to conclude negotiations on the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS), which it said had lingered for about 13 years, while ensuring that JOHESU/AHPA members were not shortchanged in ongoing collective bargaining negotiations. The conference also called for speedy construction of the Pharmacy House at Victoria Island through a developer under a well-structured timeline, while directing the PSN leadership to address outstanding entitlements of debenture subscribers and regularise the documentation of its properties. It further endorsed a one-time support contribution proposed by the PSN President to facilitate the society’s centenary celebrations scheduled for March 2027, challenging the planning committee to deliver what it described as the biggest professional event ever hosted in Nigeria. At the end of the conference, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba emerged as PSN President for the 2026/2027 year. Other members elected into the National Executive Committee include Pharm. Aisha Tukur Isiaku, Deputy President (North); Pharm. (Prof.) Henri A. Okeri, Deputy President (South); Pharm. Ndukwe Uma Ndukwe, National Secretary; and Pharm. Ehitare Patrick Omoarebu, Assistant National Secretary. Also elected were Pharm. Jelili Kilani Adewale, Treasurer; Pharm. Sani Ali Yusuf, Financial Secretary; Pharm. Lizette Njideka Ezenekwe, Publicity Secretary; and Pharm. (Prof.) Sunday A. Adesegun, Editor-in-Chief. The conference expressed appreciation to the Anambra State Government and residents for their hospitality and support throughout the five-day gathering. The post Drug insecurity threatens

item.title: Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job
item.description: As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike. So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson. Continue reading...

item.title: Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse
item.description: A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall. The Silicon Valley startup, Foundation Future Industries, claims it is developing and testing robots for military roles on battlefields from Ukraine to Gaza. Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC . The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak , supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago. This comes as Pathak and Foundation’s leadership are still looking to raise funding to support a $3 billion valuation, based on their promise to develop a humanoid robot ready for combat duty and capable of wielding various weapons. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2027: Focus on issues, stop dancing at rallies, Pawpaw tells politicians
item.description: Nollywood actor Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has urged Nigerian politicians to stop turning campaign rallies into entertainment shows, insisting that Nigerians need competent leaders who can deliver good governance. Iheme made the call in a post on his Instagram page on Monday, where he criticised the practice of politicians dancing on stage during campaign rallies. He urged political office seekers to use campaign platforms to showcase their achievements, demonstrate their capacity to lead and explain their plans to Nigerians, rather than engaging in choreography to entertain supporters. The actor said Nigerians needed competence, good governance and purposeful leadership, not political hype and entertainment. “We don’t need choreography. We need competence. We don’t need hype men. We need good governance. We don’t need entertainers. We need leaders,” he wrote. He challenged politicians to tell Nigerians what they had achieved and what they intended to do if elected. “Show us what you have done. Tell Nigerians what you will do. You are not going for Grammy,” he said. Iheme also warned politicians against dancing on campaign stages, declaring: “I don’t want to see you guys’ dance on stage again. Be careful.” The post 2027: Focus on issues, stop dancing at rallies, Pawpaw tells politicians appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: A Collage Showing 49 Drill Holes Made by NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover
item.description: 1 Min Read A Collage Showing 49 Drill Holes Made by NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover PIA26802 Credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Photojournal Navigation Science Photojournal A Collage Showing 49 Drill… Photojournal Home Photojournal Search Latest Content Galleries Feedback RSS About Downloads A Collage Showing 49 Drill Holes Made by NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover JPEG (13.80 MB) Description This collage shows 49 drill holes captured by NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover as of November 2026. Each hole represents a sample collected from rocks on the Martian surface; Curiosity’s drill, located on the end of its robotic arm, drops pulverized rock samples into instruments in its belly that analyze their composition. These images were taken by the Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), a camera that is also located on the end of the rover’s robotic arm. Each hole has a diameter of 0.63 inches (16 millimeters). Curiosity was built by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which is managed by Caltech in Pasadena, California. JPL leads the mission on behalf of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate in Washington as part of NASA’s Mars Exploration Program portfolio. MAHLI was built by Malin Space Science Systems in San Diego. item.title: Trump says he needs funding for air traffic control after ground stop
item.description: US ​President ​Donald Trump, pressed on a ​technology ‌failure ⁠that ‌grounded thousands of ⁠flights last week, ​on ‌Monday told reporters ‌that ​the government needed funding for upgrade ​to ​air traffic ​control equipment. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Sheldon Jacobson, Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois. He explains that "the Republicans have had full control of the House and the Senate since the President came in. They controlled everything. If they needed the money and wanted the money they could have approved the money. The fact that they didn't, in the the different bills that have been passed, suggests that it's more than just money that is going on here".

item.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
item.description: A hidden defect in Microsoft's cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company's history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft's report lists the incident's final status as "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." Microsoft's preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14. The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft's cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft's incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company's status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report , and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft's service-health updates . Read full article Comments

item.title: Switzerland roll over sorry Scotland to increase the pressure on Pocognoli
item.description: A match that should have been about 103 was instead about four. Andy Robertson is due acclaim for becoming the most capped player in Scotland’s history but how the full-back will wish the moment had arrived in different circumstances. A second-string Switzerland team pulled Scotland apart, raising further and significant questions about the suitability of Sébastien Pocognoli to carry out the job his paymasters boldly entrusted him with. Scottish FA giddiness about Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke, a hugely successful leader of the national team, is looking increasingly ridiculous. “I don’t think you’ve got time in international football,” said Robertson as dust settled here. Ouch. Continue reading...

item.title: Infoblox customer and staff data exposed in Sharepoint breach
item.description: Networking and security firm Infoblox is investigating a third-party breach that allowed crims to access sensitive customer and staff data. "Infoblox is investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor,” a company spokesperson confirmed to The Register . According to sources, the compromised third-party data migration vendor had trusted access to Infoblox's SharePoint system, and the intruders used this vendor’s accounts and access to exfiltrate data directly from Microsoft SharePoint. This data included configuration information related to some customer's NIOS (Network Identity Operating System) deployments. These are saved snapshots of customers’ network data, such as DNS, DHCP configurations, Grid databases, and reporting logs, that can be used to fully recover the appliance or grid in case of a system failure or faulty upgrade. The intruders also stole employee data during the break-in. According to an email CEO Scott Harrell sent to employees, which The Register has seen, compromised employee details include financial information such as direct deposit details, contact info, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers for employees and dependents. Upon discovering the breach, Infoblox “immediately activated” its incident response procedures, and took steps to contain the incident, including hiring outside cybersecurity experts, the spokesperson said. “We have sent notifications about this security event and are providing support and guidance as appropriate,” the Infoblox spokesperson told us. “Based on our investigation to date, we have no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. Our priority is to fully investigate and resolve this issue." Affected staff received a $100 "spot bonus" to buy password management services, and were warned to be "especially alert for phishing, vishing, fraud, or other suspicious communications." Infoblox also gave employees and their dependents free credit monitoring and identity protection for two years. Infoblox declined to answer our more detailed questions about the compromise, including the type of data exposed, and how many employees and customers might be affected. The Register will update this story as we learn more about the breach.®

item.title: [VIDEO] 2027: Obi Won’t Get Up To Six Million Votes, Won’t Win Lagos — YPP’s Agada
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Young Peoples Party (YPP) for the 2027 general election, Peter Agada, has said that a former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, will not secure up to 30 per cent of the six million votes he got in the 2023 presidential election. Agada stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today . He said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, who was of the Labour Party (LP) in 2023, won in Lagos due to the support received from different groups, including members of the #EndSARS group, youths, and workers. ﻿ He, however, said Obi would not win in Lagos in the forthcoming presidential election. While assessing the administration of President Bola Tinubu, Agada said that though he supports Tinubu’s removal of the fuel subsidy, he has a problem with the President not targeting the real end users and subsidising the product. He also said that Nigeria is losing about 70 per cent of its revenue to overbloated contracts. He also described the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway ₦1trn budget as overbloated, saying that he would construct one kilometre of the road for ₦750 million or ₦800 million. Asked whether he was part of the proposed coalition to unseat President Tinubu, Agada said no one had approached him. Watch the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] 2027: Obi Won’t Get Up To Six Million Votes, Won’t Win Lagos — YPP’s Agada appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
item.description: null On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there. (Image credit: SETI) Why it mattered The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute. "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's." The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University . The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI. As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13. The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also b eamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Rogue AI: California sues OpenAI over "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks
item.description: The US state of California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks, accusing the ChatGPT maker of knowingly testing dangerous advanced AI models without adequate safeguard. Meanwhile, the US Commerce Department has tightened rules over the export of US technology, aiming to close a loophole around remote access to advanced AI chips.

item.title: Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch
item.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase. It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable. Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did. The 33 Raptor engines of SpaceX's Starship V3 rocket during its test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench. Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies. Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II , with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away. EOS R5 Mark II: $3999 This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling. Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review . View Deal Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas, as a bird passes on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space , while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase. Super Heavy (top) performs a boostback burn after stage separation as Ship 42 (bottom) fires its engines on its way to space. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) That return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase. Super Heavy descends back toward Texas on Nov.

item.content:encoded: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase. It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable. Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did. The 33 Raptor engines of SpaceX's Starship V3 rocket during its test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench. Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies. Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II , with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away. EOS R5 Mark II: $3999 This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling. Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review . View Deal Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas, as a bird passes on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space , while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase. Super Heavy (top) performs a boostback burn after stage separation as Ship 42 (bottom) fires its engines on its way to space. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) That return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase. Super Heavy descends back toward Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Super Heavy flies back toward Texas, firing its engines to slow its descnet on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Super heavy performed its landing burn above the Gulf of Mexico before cutting its engines for a brief moment and exploding in a giant fireball. Super Heavy flies back toward Texas, firing its engines to slow its descnet on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) This was an intentional detonation, courtesy of the vehicle's flight termination system. Three-panel image showing Super Heavy's landing burn, engine cutoff and subsequent explosion. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) Ship continued on to low Earth orbit , where it deployed a payload of 26 upgraded Starlink Version 3 satellites . It was the second batch of V3 Starlinks delivered during Starship’s recent flight tests, each of which has added what SpaceX says is the equivalent of 10 Falcon 9 Starlink V2 satellite launches worth of data capacity to its orbital constellation. Flight 15 was also Starship's second-ever mission to orbit, and its longest so far. Ship spent nearly a full day in orbit, circling Earth a total of 14 times. During its jaunt in space, the spacecraft cleared three separate check points, which allowed SpaceX the opportunity to divert the vehicle for an ocean splashdown if needed, and finally was given the green light to attempt the first-ever Ship tower catch. SpaceX's Starship V3 rocket launches on a test flight from Starbase, Texas on May 22, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) At approximately 4:18 p.m. EST (2018 GMT, 3:18 p.m. local time in Texas) on Saturday (Nov. 14), the spacecraft broke through the cloud cover that blanketed the skies above Starbase as onlookers watched its bellyflop plunge toward the ground. Moments after becoming visible, Ship ignited its engines for a flip and burn maneuver, which oriented it upright and swung its trajectory into the tightening grip of the chopstick arms of Starbase's "Mechazilla" launch tower. Starship upper stage approaches the launch tower in Starbase, Texas on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) After a slight sway back and forth suspended above Earth in Mechazilla's embrace, Ship came to a complete rest, hanging motionless as a historic milestone in SpaceX’s pursuit of fully reusable spaceflight. Starship upper stage lowers into the launch tower in Starbase, Texas on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) The six Raptor 3 engines that powered Ship 42's return are seen as the vehicle hangs by the arms of the "Mechazilla" launch tower arms. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) It hung there overnight as engineers, and even SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , inspected the spacecraft. Ship was lowered on Sunday (Nov. 15) and transported back to SpaceX's Starbase hanger bay for further checkouts. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) SpaceX has not yet said whether Ship 42 will fly again, but its return gives engineers a chance to examine how the spacecraft held up through launch, nearly a day in orbit and atmospheric reentry. Starship hangs, caught by its launch tower on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Those findings will help inform upcoming flights as SpaceX ramps up production to continue testing Starship's capabilities. Starship hangs, caught by its launch tower on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner)

item.title: 2027 Elections: ‘Nigerians Have Been Rejecting Him,’ Segun Sowunmi Faults Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: A Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain, Segun Sowunmi, has criticised African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s repeated bids for Nigeria’s presidency, claiming that Nigerians have consistently rejected his ambition at the polls. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Responding to a question about Atiku’s belief that he is better positioned than President Bola Tinubu to govern Nigeria, Sowunmi said the former vice president should reconsider his ambition. “Well, he’s been saying that for a while, and Nigerians have been rejecting him,” he said. FILES: Segun Sowunmi on Channels Television’s Politics Today “If you have done elections the number of times Waziri (Atiku) has done, there is something he himself must consider. At what point in time does he expect younger, sharper northern people to get tired or be fatigued at running around with him?” he asked. North Presidency Calculations The PDP chieftain, who was a spokesperson for the Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign Organisation in 2023, also questioned the former vice president’s political calculations, noting that the North had already produced a president who governed for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari. He further questioned Atiku’s candidacy under the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following a Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the caretaker committee led by former Senate President David Mark. The November 5 judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Abuja, followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the ADC, challenging the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku Abubakar is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress for the 2027 general elections. The ruling affected decisions taken by the committee, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The ADC group has rejected the judgment and appealed. Sowunmi, however, maintained that Atiku’s candidacy remained uncertain. “As at today, he is not on the ballot. Because you appeal a case you lost in the lower court, does that mean you are going to win it? The bottom line is that, as at today, he is not their candidate,” he said. He also accused Atiku of mishandling the dispute involving Gombe, describing his approach as an “emir complex”. “Emirs don’t beg, emirs don’t visit people, call others. Emirs sit at home, and everybody comes to meet them. Yes, you can be an emir, but you can’t be an emir if you are looking for a ticket in another man’s party,” he added. The post 2027 Elections: ‘Nigerians Have Been Rejecting Him,’ Segun Sowunmi Faults Atiku’s Candidacy appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi
item.description: A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Segun Sowunmi, has condemned the recent ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, expressing disappointment with security agencies over their handling of the incident. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence by protesters who chanted ‘Bamayi’ at President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade, describing such actions as undemocratic. “I am disappointed, extremely disappointed that security is allowing that kind of joke to go on under the guise of people who are running democracy,” he said. Sowunmi argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate or campaign should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence. “I expect people who have a point of view different from that of a campaign to wait until the day of election to exercise their franchise. But to be destroying people’s posters, to be carrying sticks and running up and down, that’s for barbarians, and I don’t expect any sane leader to do that,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after President Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the President’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. Watch the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: This Week’s Playlist Update Comes With Wande Coal, Seyi Shay, Olamide, Khaid & More
item.description: Seyi Shay teams up with French artist Vegedream on her new single “Love & War”, one of the standout releases in this week’s music roundup. Photo Credit: Instagram A fresh Monday means it is time to clear out last week’s queue and make room for the sounds shaping Nigerian music right now. From Wande Coal reuniting with Juls and Patoranking linking up with Olamide for a musical salute to Lagos, to Khaid bridging generations with Fuji legend Saheed Osupa , Spyro delivering a quick dancefloor starter, and Seyi Shay trading English and French verses with Vegedream , there is plenty to keep your headphones busy over the next few days. Wande Coal – “Kowope” Kicking things off is Wande Coal , who reunites with British-Ghanaian producer Juls on “Kowope”, marking their first collaboration since the hit “So Mi So”. The new single is also Wande Coal’s first solo release since he put out his 15-track album KING COAL in June. This time, the pair lean into warm, percussion-led Afropop, with lyrics centred on wealth,celebration and abundance. Ahead of its release on 12 November 2026, Wande Coal gave fans a taste of what was coming with a video staged as an owambe celebration inside a banking hall—a fitting preview for a song that takes its cues from the festive side of Nigerian life. ﻿ Patoranking featuring Olamide – “Welcome to Lagos” Keeping that celebratory mood going, Patoranking and Olamide join forces on “Welcome to Lagos” to give Nigeria’s commercial capital its own musical tribute. The Afro-dancehall collaboration captures the city’s familiar mix of hustle,nightlife and everyday movement, with both artists bringing their distinct sounds to the record. Patoranking opens with his dancehall delivery, setting the pace before Olamide takes over with Yoruba verses rooted in the city’s street culture.Released on 10 November 2026 alongside an official music video, the track gives two of Nigerian music’s established names a chance to celebrate the city that continues to inspire countless songs. ﻿ Khaid featuring King Dr. Saheed Osupa – “Yasin” Switching lanes from contemporary street anthems to a meeting of two musical eras, Khaid takes an unexpected turn on “Yasin” alongside Fuji veteran King Dr. Saheed Osupa . The song brings Khaid’s contemporary Afrobeats melodies together with Osupa’s traditional Fuji vocals and talking-drum rhythms, giving both artists room to draw on their distinct musical styles. An official lyric video followed on 14 November 2026. With this collaboration, Khaid steps beyond the sound audiences may be most familiar with, while Osupa brings his unmistakable Fuji influence to a new musical setting. ﻿ Spyro – “Kpan Kpan” If you are looking to pick up the tempo even further, Spyro keeps things firmly on the dancefloor with “Kpan Kpan”, a two-minute, 19-second Afropop release produced by Colonel Tyemmy . The track is built around bouncy percussion and a hook that is easy to pick up, making it a straightforward party selection. Released on 13 N
